text: Service was ok. Good deals. But the staff was very loud and unprofessional. They were the loudest in the restaurant. Eating while working. Just being generally obnoxious. Will not be going back.

Great service but terrible food.  
We were staying at a nearby hotel and were referred to Earls.  The food didn't seem fresh and lacked flavor. It was parallel to something you could make at home from inexpensive frozen food with a deep fryer.  
We didn't finish our food and went to a nearby 7-11 to get something far superior.

I went in yesterday for a lomi lomi massage that I bought from Groupon with a friend. We both loved the experience :) sometimes with Groupon you can be treated like a second class citizen but not here! The ladies were polite and informative. I'm pregnant and Trisha did a wonderful job in accommodating my belly, she has very strong hands which I love. This was my first time having a lomi lomi massage and it was really relaxing but she still got into my tight spots.The place is so peaceful and relaxing and it smelt wonderful, I never wanted to leave! I will definitely be back. Thank you for the wonderful experience. We felt so pampered :)

Ong Hanoi Fried Chicken just opened yesterday, by the same owners and same building as Jack's Burgers.  We tried the individual dinners tonight and this chicken is fabulous.  Crispy exterior with a heavenly glaze hides glorious moist, tender, juicy flavorful marinated chicken.  We did takeout and it was a huge hit, from crotchety grandpa to 9 yr old grandson. It's a small place more suited to takeout.  Chicken dinners, meatballs, chicken wings, spring rolls, iced coffee, artichoke iced tea, fresh made pickles.  The dinner includes a connected leg/thigh piece and breast, rice and pickles.  Large meal that I couldn't finish (leftovers for tomorrow). Best fried chicken I've ever had and not greasy at all. A delightful addition to the north west area of the city!

Great addition to St.Albert!

We accidentally showed up at 3pm when they were closed, but the guy running it kept it open for us and was nice enough to make our order.   What a great place!!! You have to try their wings and meatballs.  They use rice flour for the chicken and WOW is it great.

Will definitely be back!!

Great service, meh food. My steak and shrimp were both undercooked, asparagus overcooked, garlic mash was dry. Draught beer was good as was dessert...but I can hit a pub for a less expensive pint and DQ for dessert.

Give it a miss.

This is a great gym, in that it's not very crowded, there's lots of cardio machines, the staff is friendly and there's complimentary tea and coffee and hair dryers. Do I feel it is worth the price tag? Not particularly, but I guess if you're willing to pay big bucks for a less crowded feel, then this is the place for you.

My best friend and I  (who are both almost 40) went to Earls in St Albert about a month ago. We sat in the lounge and ordered the Dynamite Rolls, fries and beers (I know, strange combination....we're fun like that!). Anyway, we were discussing some personal trials we had both been through lately and ended up a little teary eyed. The waitress kindly, without drawing any attention to us, dropped off some tissues. I was grateful for that! But then, the Manager came by and brought us both a shot (shooter) and dropped them off with a "I thought you could use this". 
So to Earls and to that Manager/Waitress....
I was so impressed by you. It wasn't about the free shot, it wasn't about the tissue.....it was about the respect and kindness you showed both of us. I was so grateful for your service that night (in a province where it's hard to find good service these days), that I still think back and smile. I'm not an Earls regular but I certainly will be now. All because of one small little gesture that meant A LOT! Thank you.

Did they change the chicken taco recipe? cause they were not good today. No slaw. Too much feta. Some weird veggie on top that looked like pickled ginger but tasted of nothing. Disappointing but I won't give up.

This Earls is pretty disappointing. I went out with a big group for my sisters Birthday, and it was just so "meh".

The service was horriable...extreamly slow, and not once was I asked if I wanted another drink. 

The food when it finally came was only ok..defonately not worth the price you pay. I had the chicken jeera curry. And it was small and pretty much something I make at home. 

My sister (the Birthday girl) had her entre order mixed up and ended up with something completely different then she ordered..they did bring her the right one in the end. But there was no real apology and no "compensation"..no free drink, nothing! It was her Birthday!

It was SO expensive too..like for what it was. I'm not rushing back to Earl's in a hurry.

The Dynamite rolls are! We frequent Earls with usually a short wait but worth it. We find the food well prepared, service is better than average. Don't be disappointed with poor reviews if you have never been.
Great variety!

Cute little restaurant with graffiti on the wall.  I stopped by for a quick bite to go. The server was really sweet, giving recommendations and making sure I was comfortable, assuring the order will be done soon, offering water etc.  I ordered the bahn mi with pork and the fried chicken with rice.  The bahn mi was A-Ok but smaller than what I'd expected / what I'd get at other places.  The chicken had good flavour but too bad was a little pink on the inside :(
My family and I had a wonderful dinner at Earls yesterday. The prices are a little high for us but the food and service could not have been better. Well done!

Nope.  Can't make me go back.  I've been there a couple of times now, and I'm always disappointed with the food and the service.  This last time, the rice on my sushi roll was very under cooked.  I was thanked for my feedback, but it was in that of "Ya, I'll just go file that info for ya" kind of way.  Way over priced for the quality of food you get.  This is in the same category as Moxie's, only half as good.

I had been going to this gym for years and year..around 8 in total. But the prices kept going up and up; and the classes slowly stopped being free. The cost was ridiculous in the end, way to much for a student. So I switched over to servus..pay way less a month, and get so many more services, Plus with Servus you get access to the pool there and Fountain Park Pool, I get so much more now and pay way less a month..and the "free" muffins, toast, and apples just don't make up for the large price; it just doesn't do it for me. And I know they offer RUSK shampoo and conditioner products, but there sooo watered down  you end up having to bring your own...like I'm fairly certain they add water to the conditioner, its so odd! SVAC needs to realize that they are a small player in the market now and adjust the prices accordingly!

Ong is the latest fried chicken joint to open up in town. This one specializes in Hanoi style fried chicken and is owned by the same crew that runs Jack's Burger Shack and Cerdo Tacos.

We came on a Wednesday for lunch and I was surprised to see it wasn't busy. A couple families and that was it. The murals on the wall are interesting; I liked the Vietnamese farmer working the field with his ox but the village behind the counter is also pretty.

The menu is small with them focusing on half a dozen items.

- Banh mi ($7.00) - decent and even had a nice kick to it; sadly, it's a small and average. Go to Chinatown and get one for $4.00 instead.
- Pho sot vang ($9.00) - this was the best dish we ordered. Hearty, homemade, comforting broth that I imagine your Vietnamese mom/grandma would cook for you. The beef was tender, juicy and you get a plethora of noodles. Perfect to share; just ask for an extra bowl.
- 2 piece chicken ($13.00) - the thigh was moist and flavourful but the breast was quite dry. We liked the sweet, sticky sauce but I thought they could have used more of a bread coating. 
The side of rice is tinnyyyyyyyy. For the price tag, you'd think they wouldn't be so stingy. It's plain rice...yeesh.

Overall, decent but everything is a few dollars overpriced. At least St. Albert is slowly getting more ethnic restaurants so chalk that up in the plus column.

This is review is for the PlayCare/Birthday Party option.

Wow!  The PlayCare area here is freaking awesome!  From a rock climbing wall to zip line to slides that were fast enough yet safe enough to keep both my 3 & 6 year old happy, this place has it all!  There is a crafting room as well as pretend area (think kid kitchens, etc.) and a toddler area.  The variety of play options here was incredibly diverse and the best I've ever seen in a gym.

Washrooms located right inside the play area and the coffee/snack area has a viewing area to watch the kiddos if you like.

While I don't plan on joining the gym here anytime soon (more than double the fee of GoodLife and the like) I can definitely see the appeal.

The entire area was completely pristine from top to bottom and the staff were friendly and the kids felt immediately comfortable with them.

Two Thumbs Up for the PlayCare (also does birthday parties) at Sturgeon Valley Athletic Club!

I always like to eat local. Of course to support local businesses but I also find that they have more unique food on the menu. We were in StAlbert last minute and decided to go to Earls I was expecting them to have a better variation. They had unique things on their drink menu but their food menu was same old same old. They are lacking vegetarian and vegan options. I ended up Ordering soup and salad. I was actually pleasantly surprised the soup and salad were quite good. The service was friendly and my friends seem to enjoy their food 
I just wish they had a more unique menu. If I could I would've given a 3 1/2 star

Food is always a good earls standard never been bad.  Nice atmosphere. 

Service is just  so so.....nothing to rave about but if that isn't a huge concern you will be happy

I am confused if I like Earls. The various drinks are amazing but in my mind the wine is way over priced. The meals I like, I really like and the others not so much! Like the spinach dip appy, dip is soooo good and the bread with it is meh at best. The cajun special menu on now is great! I will admit damn both the servers and clients are easy on the eyes! The manager coming around with wine samples was nice and the service was great! 3.5 / 5!

I recently moved to the area from California and wanted to join a local gym because I'm a runner and it's obviously too cold for a recent transplant to run outside. I was debating between Sturgeon and Servus (because of their indoor track) for a membership. Took tours at both places and Sturgeon gave me a trial for 2 weeks where I wasn't offered one at Servus. 

My husband was a SVAC member back in time and highly recommended Sturgeon because of the amenities and his past experiences with the club. I signed up for one month and boy was he right! I've gone 11 out of 16 times since I've signed up. Here are my accolades for this facility: 

Variety: Even though this club doesn't have an indoor track they sure make up for it with their diverse selection of equipment, machines and classes. In the past I was a runner/free weights/weight machine/balance ball person, but I feel comfortable enough to try workouts that I usually wouldn't have touched (mostly to surprise my muscles with new workouts). Here are a few examples: row machine, various balance boards, kettle bells, TRX and then a TRX class and insanity class. Let's say my muscles have limited time to recover because of all the things SVAC has to offer. 

Atmosphere: First off, the staff here is great. The evening receptionists and duty supervisors are really helpful and friendly. Evelyn asked me post workout how my workout went and I told her I've been experimenting with TRX for the first time. She recommended a new TRX class they added for March and recommended I go to it for more guidance. Very thoughtful! 

Lisa (TRX) and Keri (Insanity) were very energetic and passionate instructors. They keep the energy up and are very thorough with explaining the exercises. If you haven't tried it, signup, they're great but be prepared to work! 


Cleanliness: In regards to the last review, this place is pristine. Maybe it's because I go in the evening closer to closing time but I've seen the staff clean the windows on a Friday night, replace the rags to wipe down machines, constantly doing laundry, mop the studio floors, replace the hot thermals of coffee/water for the next day and wipe down machines when they weren't in use. Plus I see the staff routinely walk through the female locker room to make sure everything is in order. 

Extra Amenities: I've been to various clubs in California that have great amenities but I have to say this is by far THE best one with all the bells and whistles. There's a large lounge to relax pre/post workout with many chairs and tables including free coffee/tea. They offer bfast in the morning (never tried it but that's always nice). They have 2 different towels for members to use: on the gym floor and another for shower use. Many many magazines. If you're on a cardio machine, a staff member walks around and offers a rolled cold washcloth for your convenience. Pamphlets of each trainer with their photo, credentials and overall experience. 

Women's Lounge: There are various parts throughout the locker room where you can perch and fix your hair/makeup. They include glasses cleaner, Qtips, mouthwash, lotion, hairdryers and curlers. A 4 person max sauna to detox in!! A lounge area to watch TV, haha, there are 4 chairs and my favorite part... an electric massage chair! Full body massage = 7 mins. 


I have one suggestion to management. There are more combo code lockers than bring your own lock lockers in the women's lounge. Please consider replacing some of them for people like me that can only remember one set of numbers. 


Other available amenities I didn't mention because I haven't tried or they were additional $$. 
-pod machine
-Pilates reformer (will try the demo soon!)
-Connected to True Balance Spa ... great prices for massages! 
-Kid's Play Area (don't have kids)

Overall, I like to wind down and relax after an intense workout session so for me it's worth the extra dollars for all the SVAC goodies.

Great place for a gathering! Beers were well reviewed by my coworkers (sadly I can't enjoy them quite yet but I will be back with others that can) and the space is beautifully laid out with handcrafted tables. As this was a private event, we didn't try the food onsite but was great that they accommodated the large group to bring in a food truck. We also enjoyed a brewery tour before our official portion of the evening. Thanks for being such a great venue to host a very important gathering.

I frequent many Earls locations. The food here is standard earls food, which is good. Not amazing, but consistently good. The atmosphere/layout varies between locations. This one is pretty open and one half is the lounge and other half is the dining room. Smaller than most other earls which doesn't really matter since the majority of times I have been to this one there hasn't been a ton of people in the restaurant. Its probably one of the better restaurants  in St. Albert. Its not liking going out to downtown restaurants as this location seems to still be a more quiet family restaurant.

We went during happy hour. The place wasn't crazy busy. I don't know if they didn't have enough staff on or if our server was just not attentive. We had to wait quite a while to get menus. And once she brought our food we didn't see her again until the end of the meal. I like when servers let you be, but I think they should check in at least once in case you need something.

I've been to Earls several times over the years. And for the most part they have decent service along with better than average food.  However, the one thing I find is that it's always hit and miss, for both food and service.  You go there once, you get great service, the next time, less than admirable.  

Lately the food has been less than desirable.  Went to the St. Albert version on Boxing day for a bit of a family outing.  There were 8 of us, so we weren't a small group, but not a large one either.  Service was good, however the food was not.  Had ordered a burger and fries.  Usually not a difficult meal to make.  Fries came out cold, and hamburger was thin, dry and cold.  Bun was dry as well.  They did execute the order correctly (without onion and pickle) but past that it was sub-standard.  Had asked for pepper since it's not supplied on the tables (only salt) and instead I got ketchup.  Server never came back around again after that. hmmmff.  

Overall it's a nice place to go with a clean look and fresh design, but I'd prefer a place that looked a little less trendy for better food.  

It'll be a while before I venture back again.

When you step inside and make your order, sit back and get ready for your tastebuds to take a trip! The food is simple but delicious and layered with flavour. If your not sure what to order the helpful staff will make sure you get just the right meal.
Hit this place up on your next trip downtown

This French style bakery is much like the famous Duchess Bakery without the huge line ups.  I visited on a quiet weekday afternoon and was impressed with the selection of baked deliciousness that looked at me through the display case.  I chose an eclair and a truffle.  I am a bit particular when it comes to baked goods.  Both were of excellent quality and seemed fresh.  I did not see the price of the eclairs but the truffles were $1.25 each.   Seating is very comfortable and elegant with French provincial style couches and tables.  Now for areas that can be improved, the number one area would be customer service.  The girl who served us was somewhat unapproachable and seemed stand-off ish.  After we ordered, she seemed to mellow out.  Later on, a customer came in and I observed that the customer waited an unacceptably long time before anyone came out of the back to assist her. The same employee who served us was somewhat abrasive towards this customer when she asked a question.  Again, the employee mellowed out as soon as the customer ordered.  Besides an
Improvement in customer service, I found the menu on the mirrors very difficult to read.  Hopefully I'll be back one day and see a more friendly interaction with employees.  Based solely on
product quality, this place deserves a 4 star review.

Earls is one of our go-to places in St Albert when we're looking for tasty, dependable food that's sometimes a bit out there. 

Our latest visit was a two-for... We went for dinner prior to going to see my daughter in the latest SACT show at the Arden, and then a group of us came back after the performance for some post-show nibblies, and both times we had great food.

First, the service level was excellent - even though our server Shauna had only been there a few months, she had obviously been well - trained (timing of visits tour table, quick responses for special requests), and she was also very personable and engaging.

The food itself was pretty quick even though they were busy so kudos to the kitchen team too. At the table we started w a spinach and Asiago dip (better get an extra  order of bread so you can get it all! :), then had salmon, chicken wings and fries, a bi-bim-bop (Korean rice bowl w an egg that finished cooking at your table), and some Cajun chicken. Although I did t get a chance to taste all of the items, at one time or another I think I've had each of them and they're all delicious! Salmon still juicy, the rice bowl very flavorful, and the chicken had just the right amount of spicing too. Add to all that a decent selection of wine for whatever grabs you, and we were almost thoroughly set! The only downside of the entire night was that they had a mix-up in the kitchen earlier in the day so we couldn't get a seasonal fave, the gingerbread dessert... Because the mix-up had happened that morning, I would have thought they would have had it sorted out by evening.

On the return trip we had our usual faves - spinach dip and wings again (well we did have new people at the table so they needed some yummies too!), dry ribs, and yam fries and again don't forget the dip! 

Overall a great night; fantastic food and service and a relaxed environment where we could reconnect w friends and family.

Color me impressed! I've had the pleasure of eating here twice, both times I ordered the 2-piece chicken meal.
They were in the middle of revamping the menu on my second visit and had to break the news to me that the 2 piece meal was no longer offered. The gentleman I spoke to on the phone, however, made a substitution for me and told me I could have chicken wings instead. Sure! Why not?
I opened my takeout box to discover 5 or 6 massive chicken wings alongside the rice and homemade pickles that it usually comes with. I was super surprised to see the sheer amount of food I got for $11.50 (seemingly reduced cost). I had enough food to last me for two meals.
The customer service has always been phenomenal on top of this, which just makes for an overall awesome experience! This has become my go-to chicken restaurant in St. Albert.

I won't waist times here ,here we go ! ....... happy hours are great ,best value in town :) , but now the service ..... ok it's a typical millennial new generation of service industry people there , just as any other corporations........always on the cellphones ......careless....will not take a extra step to make our experience enjoyable and god ! Can someone pls teach those kids social skills ?!?!  Enough said and thank u !

Yum! We don't usually ever come to St Albert (south side for life!), but we had tickets to an event at the Arden Theatre so I checked yelp to see what was near by.

After checking the online menu of both Earls and Joey (including nutritional value - New Years resolution still going strong), I decided to book a little reservation at Earls and get myself some steak!

Predictably, the place was hoppin' on a Saturday night, but we got seated right away and our friendly waitress came to offer us some beverages. The wine was divine and the steak was super yummy.

My husband enjoyed the fish and chips and obviously I checked out the bathrooms - all clean and pretty! Overall, great weekend spot - don't forget your reservation!

My first visit here was for a pedicure that I got on Groupon. I was able to book an appointment within a couple of days of phoning and their internet booking system worked flawlessly. I received both a confirmation phone call and an e-mail confirming my appointment. My pedicure was perfect.  When I left my appointment my feet felt like I was walking on clouds. I have psoriasis on the bottoms of my feet and they had not felt this good in years.  There was a large selection of high end polishes and colours and I chose one called pink flamingo. I actually had several strangers complement me on how pretty my feet looked.  That has never happened to me before!

The chicken here was absolutely delicious! We tried the chicken pieces with jack's fries which were the best I've tried as well as the 2 piece chicken with rice-so good! The spring rolls were flavorful & the service was so friendly. I would definitely recommend :)

I have to say I really enjoyed my experience here! I at first had problems finding the place and the lady on the phone was helpful. Because I had problems finding it I was late for my appointment but they were super understanding and still gave me great customer service. I had deep tissue massage with Melanie and it was the best one I have had yet! She's super knowledgable and really helps you understand how simple tricks at home can improve your life.  I was able to get into an appointment for my next visit no problem, and they offer insurance receipts! I love it and would defiantly recommend this place to my friends and family :)

I have been to Earls at several locations but I am definitely not a regular. I had always thought they had a fairly diverse menu and decent enough quality. We had a gift card from a close friend and thought we should give them another try.

Friday night we thought we would go for dinner before heading to the movies. We got there at 5:45pm thinking we would beat the dinner rush. WRONG! Half the tables in the restaurant were empty and there was a 45 MINUTE WAIT! I have worked in the restaurant business and know there are only a couple reasons so many tables would be empty at what appeared to be peak time: either they have so few wait staff they can't run the business, or the manager is too afraid of "slamming" the kitchen that he/she won't seat the whole restaurant at one time. They could also have had a big reservation but that would not be a very smart business move for peak Friday dinner time. To say the least we did not stay on Friday night.

So, Saturday we had a long day cleaning up the yard for fall, and thought "Hey, lets go back and give Earls another shot." Well, we arrived and were seated right away. Awesome! The restaurant seemed fairly full, with lots of kids (odd considering I would not really figure Earls as a top spot for kids.) Our waitress was nice, but it took her over 5 minutes to get to our table to say hi.

They do not have "real" menus - just printed paper that looks like it should be single-use. Ours had definitely seen many hands and had been used as place mats too. Speaking of the menus - what happened to all the food? They have several categories, but everything seems to be the same recycled ingredients. There is sweet chili sauce or chili rub on pretty much all of the menu. Under "Mains" where I'd expect to see a variety of fish, poultry, beef, etc. there are THREE items. Ribs, ribs/chicken combo, and fish and chips. There is a separate steak section, but come on, thats pretty pathetic.

My wife ended up getting soup and salad, and I got the pecan chicken salad. My salad was $17, and was worth about $8. The chicken was okay but the amount of crust it had on it, you would expect some flavour. The greens were about one cup of arugula, and it had about one cup of tzatziki tasting dressing smothered all over the plate. There were a few pear slices and a few pickled beets too.

As we ate our meal we saw the section getting emptier and emptier. The tables sat dirty and not made up for new diners. By the time we were done there were close to 20 empty seats around us. We could see there was a wait at the door as well, so we really did not know what was going on. As we were leaving we saw what looked lie about 10 people with party gifts, so maybe they had reserved a whole section?

So, to wrap this up all I can say is we will not return to Earls voluntarily. The food was overpriced and under-seasoned.  (We had two glasses of house wine, two salads, and split a piece of pie for $77) The service, although friendly, was extremely slow. We cannot understand their seating strategy at all. They should not be taking party reservations in a restaurant of that size - I can only imagine the quality of food and service for a group larger than four.

Groupon brought me here for an awesome pedicure (and lets be honest, that often does not happen with Groupon).  She did an excellent job with everything and seemed to understand that I was exhausted after a long day of work and not in the mood for small talk.  Very relaxing and the esthetician was lovely.  I am glad Groupon introduced me to this great little spa, it's close to my house and I did not know it existed until now but I will definitely be going again!

We just finished a tremendous East Coast themed dinner! The mussels in white wine were outstanding, the popcorn shrimp generously portioned and make sure you try the East Coast Iced Tea! Incredible! We'll be back

This place is absolutely delicious. i found it through skip the dishes and it absolutely covers the delectable dessert cravings. The only reason I chose 4 instead of 5 stars is that that prices are on the higher end. But so worth the price tag haha So for me it will be a once in awhile thing. Today I got their carrement chocolat, vanilla, lemon poppyseed, strawberry maple and cotton candy macorons, and their caramel milkshake. The first one was so rich that I could only eat a couple bites haha and that means it's the best there is that I have found in 20 years lol ladies?? If you are craving chocolate something once a month? I highly recommend this dessert!! Pics of the little cake/mouse included in this post. The Macarons are simply perfect. They melt in the mouth. They are vibrantly coloured and one is more than enough :) they are not overly sweet so that's a huge plus haha huge shout out to this hidden away dessert heaven. Well done.

It's mostly just the service. Earls has the same quality control when it comes to their menu right across Canada I believe. But holy smokes,  try to get decent service at this location. Its horrible really.  So by the end of your visit, the usually decent food is cold and unappealing because your 4th request for condiments has gone unanswered or the coffee or wine you wanted to accompany your meal is non existant because the server is no where to be found.  I actually contemplated calling the restaurant from my cell phone on my last visit, but instead walked to the server station at the back of the restaurant myself to put in my order. Im done.

Macarons & Goodies second location recently opened up in St. Albert. 

Boasting over 21 flavors of Macarons and dozens of other house made French specialties! 

Faves for me include the Lavender honey, raspberry, & salted caramel Macarons.  Close runner up to pistachio!  I have yet to make my way through tasting all 21 varieties so an update will be required ;-). 

The quality was much fresher here than what I had bought at the downtown YEG location - traffic was busy here. 

Macarons & Goodies is a welcomed addition to the St. Albert downtown shopping corridor!
I've gotten two therapeutic massages here, both from Nicole, and they were awesome. The atmosphere is relaxing, the staff are warm and professional, and I will definitely be back.

I had a car accident years ago and I've had to have massages to help with my back pain. So needless to say I've been to a lot of places that gives massages. I also have to say that none of theses places ever helped me for more than a few hours. Now after going to purple lotus the first time for a massage I never want to go anywhere else. It was amazing so much so that I've had to decrease my pain medication by at least half. My life is so much better. Thank so much to the staff of purple lotus you are all amazing. BTW. Try their manicure and pedicures they last for at least three weeks
Bouncers are aggressive there friends  there hadn't even had one drink anywhere and they charged up on them demanding they get out accused them of being too drunk "" treated with no respect at all
Clinic is very basic but has a good atmosphere.  I had Tricia - might have been the best massage I've ever had.  Definitely recommend.

My boyfriend and I decided to try the 30 day trial membership here after going to Servus Place for over a year. Staff is friendly and I really like the locker rooms, but this isn't the gym for you if you basically only lift weights and do minimal cardio. It's definitely a gym for people who spend an hour on the treadmill or bike and nothing else.

The weight area is super cramped, barely enough room to walk around. If there are 3 people in the area it's way too crowded. I also noticed that a LOT of people aren't wiping their equipment down after use which is irritating. 

After some debate we decided to go back to Servus Place as we feel the facilities are cleaner, brighter, newer, air conditioned and there's always music playing!

They may only (currently) have 3 beers on tap but they are all worth sampling. The owners are very friendly and they definitely know what they are doing when it comes to brewing. Their food menu is also small but high quality. If you are a fan of craft beer then come check them out and you will not be disappointed. BTW $14 for a growler of quality craft brew is amazing and worth the trip on its own.

Excellent! Me and a couple of my girlfriends came in for some drinks on Saturday a couple of weeks ago, and had a wonderful time at Earls St.Albert. Our waitress Natasha was super friendly and attentive. Great atmosphere. One of the managers came over to check on us as well, he was also super friendly and made sure we were having a fantastic night, overall super taken care of, and the food was delicious!

My wife and I have been there twice now and have enjoyed both the food and beer selection. We were quite disappointed when the Celtic Knot closed but this place is a good alternative. We were especially impressed with both bartenders Kayla and Emma. They were both very pleasant and prompt.

Great place for a Pint!
It's my go to place for a Friday evening or a afternoon on the patio. 
Love the selection and you can take out cans or Growlers. 
Love the Tacos as well.

I am giving this cafe  a 2 because the crepes were nice but the coffee was horrible and the Macarons were stale and tasted nothing like the advertised flavour. I only mentioned the coffee to the server and she told me they never had issues with their coffee before.

This gym has advantages and disadvantages depending on what you are looking for.  I personally prefer it over any of the other gyms I have tried in the St. Albert area: Servus, World Health, etc. 

Advantages (in my opinion): 
*Free plyo and spin classes at hours that are appropriate for hitting the gym before work.  (All of the instructors are excellent.)
* Plenty of "free" perks such as Starbucks coffee and towel service.
* Lots of equipment and studios to accommodate whatever type of workout you're looking for (minus a track like Servus or Olympic weights, but that doesn't matter to me personally).
* Enough clean showers that I have never had to wait, even during the morning rush.
* Plenty of well lit, vanity space for putting on makeup/doing hair, etc.
* Friendly, helpful staff and excellent programs such as the "bodpod challenge" which you won't find at any other gym in the area.

Disadvantages (in my opinion, while noting that no gym is perfect):
* The cost.  To many people (myself included) this gym is worth the price you pay.  The target clientele of this gym is clearly not students looking for a basic gym.
* The cancellation policy (being charged for not showing up) for the free classes is only enforced if a person signs up.  Plenty of people show up without signing up and this creates problems if you are not early for class as the classes get crowded quickly and some instructors set up equipment for only the number of people who are signed up for the class.  (People who do not sign up will take these spots.) 
* The above point is more a reflection on the gym members than the gym, although instructors should be more diligent on enforcing the rules.  Generally gym members are positive and friendly, but there is often an air of entitlement with many gym members.
* Not all of the trainers will require their clients to wipe down the equipment after using it and will sometimes leave clipboards etc in the way of other people wanting to use benches etc.

Overall, I would highly recommend this gym.

Last month, I read on the Purple Lotus Facebook page that they were going to be hosting/mentoring three students from Makami College. At the end of their first year, each student has to complete 80-hours of unpaid practicum. So I booked a massage with Nicole. 

I have been having severe night-time back pain. And I'm still grieving the loss of my mom a few months ago. While Nicole couldn't fix these two things, she gave me an incredible therapeutic massage, and I walked out into the September sunshine feeling relaxed and pain free. She took my concerns seriously and suggested seeing my doctor and even got the name of a physiotherapist from Kirsty (the owner). Also, the session brought up a lot of emotion, and Nicole treated me with a lot of kindness and compassion. She really knew how to work with my energy. She knows her craft very well and I booked another appointment as she is continuing on for at least the next few months. 

A word about the studio. The rooms are quite beautiful and the sheets are like HEAVEN, I've never had a massage on sheets like these. It was very relaxing, and the temperature, lighting, and music level was perfect (although it felt like I could faintly hear someone else's music). Before I left, I bought one of the astrological nail files I noticed in the waiting area. Next time I might grab a couple more, they would make awesome stocking stuffers.

Connor's Pub is a gem in the city. 

The food is decent for what you would expect at a pub! The chicken fingers and fries are usually half price during happy hour (which seems to be always). 

The service is good. Jason is an amazing bartender who can keep up a good conversation and always has recommendations for what you should eat or drink next if you're uncertain! 

There are two pool tables which are usually always busy but are good entertainment. One thing I really enjoyed was the live band they brought in! It definitely was a highlight of the night. 

The biggest disappointment about Connor's is that the layout is spread out so it never looks busy. Because of this, it's not somewhere you go to meet new people. 

Overall, I think Connor's is doing well. I think more promotional events, more advertising and drink specials people can't resist would give it a better edge.

The location is tucked away in the corner of the industrial park, but once inside, it's warm and welcoming. It was clean and fresh, with a home-like waiting room. 
The massage was fantastic, and gave me some immediate relief of my lower back pain. 
I had a great discount from a one time groupon, but made a second appointment before I left!

I love the ambiance of the place. Everything is orderly, pretty and so tempting. I've only had the triple chocolate at the time of writing this, and it is as good, if not much better than how it looks!

I booked a pedicure at the last minute as I realized very late that my Groupon that I had purchased was going to expire within a week. My call was answered right away and I was able to get an appointment within a few days... before my Groupon expired.

Dallas was my esthetician and she did an excellent job, there were so many polish color options it was hard to choose, my feet feel amazing. 

The staff were very friendly and helpful, the location of the spa is great but a little hard to find in the dark but the staff did tell me that the illuminated sign was going to be installed soon.

I will definitely be back!

Worst experience I have had at a restaurant in a long time. We came for a quick lunch with our daughter, we waited over an hour for a ceaser salad and a chicken rice bowl. There was five groups of two people in the whole restaurant.  When we got our food the chicken on the salad was so over spiced and over cooked it was barely edible, my wives rice bowl came out without the chicken even on it, she had to wait another five minutes for that. I had heard this earls was going down hill but figured we would still try it out. Probably won't be back again unless it's just for drinks.

I find the Earls in St. Albert to be reliable.  The service can be a bit slow, but once your order is in the food comes quickly, and is consistently of good quality.  I find that the waitresses are stretched a bit thin at this location, so they don't have enough time to check in and ask if you'd like a drink refill.  However, as I said, once the food is ready it seems to appear speedily.

This Earls is a lot more casual than some in the city as well, which is a nice change.
One does not have to fly to Jolly Old for great bitter.  The ESB is exceptional.  Well done.

All I need to say is that we had an amazing server this evening, Thomas. Being a past server at a high end restaurant I am very attentive to the quality of service. He was always there before we needed him and was extremely nice to talk to. The food was also great :) Thanks!

Seems like a random location, but it's such a beautiful facility. I had a 60 minute deep tissue massage because of groupon and it was really phenomenal. The bed was heated, which you can't beat during the winter. It smelled great, was really quiet and peaceful, and Jenine was very good. ensuring that she was applying appropriate pressure throughout the massage, and then talked to me after to let me know how to improve places that were tight.
Amazing service from the bar tender. But... they ran out of certain foods. Very annoyed as it was not very busy and I asked for a few different foods but the waitress informed me that they were "out"

This would be my 2nd home if the staff were more welcoming. I think on a few occasions they were but the other occasions were truly off-putting. They do have tasty treats but the freshness is hit and miss. I like the ambiance and decor. Please up your game!

I've eaten at Earls pretty frequently over the years for various occasions. Yesterday I was visiting with my cousin and wanted to grab some breakfast, so we popped into this Earls.

I had scoped the menu ahead of time and knew I wanted to try the eggs benny because it is my faaaaavorite breakfast item, hands down. My cousin ordered the same, and his wife ordered chicken tacos and a fresh green juice (which looked amazing).

Our food came out quickly, but I could immediately see that the eggs were essentially raw. You know when you wiggle a plate and a poached egg flies around precariously like a water balloon? That. 

I asked the server if he would mind asking the kitchen to just warm them up until the whites were cooked for me (nobody wants salmonella), which he did. Some time later my meal returns with one egg cooked slightly better, but the other still raw. I didn't want to complain more, so I dug in and just planned to eat the cooked egg. When the server came around to check how things were my cousin let her know that I had been served a raw egg again. She agreed to bring me another plate, so I stopped eating. The manager brought around some complimentary Beignets (very kind) and a short time later the server came back with just two poached eggs. I was a little irritated because I had stopped eating and let my potatoes get cold, and I had to use my raw egg soaked bread to eat with the finally properly cooked eggs. And the saddest part of all- I didn't have enough hollandaise sauce!

I give the restaurant 2 stars because they did attempt to correct the situation (though quite poorly) and my cousin's wife enjoyed her meal. The ambiance is also quite nice in here. However, I certainly won't be returning for breakfast any time soon because I don't think they've figured out how to cook eggs!

My friend and I recently went to Earl's St. Albert for appetizers and a main course.

Pros
- The atmosphere was fun, relaxing and had good energy 
- The front door hosts were knowledgeable, friendly and sat us at a table quickly
-The warm spinach dip was AMAZING

Areas of improvement
- The waitress took our plates away without asking if we wanted it packed up
- The value for money isn't the best. For an average meal the customer is paying above market value prices
There's an ignorant guy server there. Rude and doesn't smile. Judges you when you order off the happy hour menu.

I am here from 10:50am till when I desire to leave. Sunday Feb 9 2020 Bartender (Sarah)is awesome she is very attentive to customers requests. Food came quick within 10mins of ordering...Country breakfast(2sunnyside eggs, sausage, 2 strips of bacon, brown beans, and 2 artists bread slices grilled) $15 sitting at the bar so sometimes quicker service.

I always see my friends having tasty drinks and meals at Earls, but I've come to realize that they don't usually come from this location.
This location has been a staple in the city for many years and is almost always busy from passing by. 
That said, I've never found the quality of the food to be too great. Most of the meals I've had over the course of those years have been either dry or bland. The burgers are so dry that my S/O only ate half his. My forager burger was okay (I ate it, obviously, cause I'm a piggy) but it was pretty bland. The fries are always the best part of the meal, but, you know, still dry and bland. The salads are expensive and the portion size looks like it's been cut right down in the last 5-7 years for the same price.
The caesars are pretty good (a little bit chunky for my liking) and the beef jerky stick is a cute garnish.
The service always meets a standard and is as it should be and the restaurant is comfortable, especially the patio portion. But I assure you that a much better meal is to be had across the street at The Celtic Knot for a similar cost, if not cheaper.

Yaaaaay! I'm so happy this is right here in my neighborhood. 
First impressions? Pretty neat looking place. I love the Victorian-style decor and the big windows. The food menu is extensive, albeit a little difficult to read. I have yet to try the meals, but I'll be sure to update my review when I do. 
As for the baked goods, everything looks delicious. I had never had a real, proper macaron before coming here, but I imagine this is exactly how they're supposed to taste. There's what seems like a million flavors to choose from, which means there's something for everyone. The lattes are lovely and will keep me coming back as well. 
Macarons & Goodies does have to contend with a neighboring cafe a few doors down, but I feel hopeful that the excellent word-of-mouth that this place has been getting so far will keep it busy!

The last few times I have been to this Earls have been quite disappointing.  A few months ago I went specifically for the Clam Chowder and they had burnt the pot but still served us the soup.  It was really gross. They were nice when we sent it back but they didn't have any other chowder to replace it.

Last night I went for a drinks and a light dinner with a few friends and the restaurant only had a few tables.  It took over 10 minutes for anyone to come by and it was almost 20 before our drinks came out.  Three of us ordered, and a forth joined who ordered around 10 minutes after.  Two meals came out, and then the meal for the late joiner came out, but my meal did not.  I ordered soup and salad and it took over 40 minutes to come out.  Once it did, it was cold and the bread was rock hard. The waitress didn't come by for 15 minutes, so instead of being able to get a hot soup, I got nothing.  They took it off my bill but I definitely went home hungry.  They were having computer issues but it didn't equate for the entire disappointing experience.  Won't be going back to this Earls that's for sure!!

I went to Endeavour Brewery for the first time on a Saturday afternoon after the farmers market and wow! The city of St. Albert has a lot of hidden gems. 

I tried a sampler of 4 different beers. They were all delicious! The price was reasonable. I believe it was about $10.50 for what I ordered. My friends and I sat on the patio and it was lovely. Not too busy and easy to physically distance from other groups as seating is limited. 

My friend tried the beer cheese and chips and said it was really tasty. The food menu appears small but let's get real, most people will go for the drinks! 

Would highly recommend and I will be returning soon!

Came here again on Sunday Feb 23 around 11:45am. Had a wonderful server named Sarah H.

Getting refills before being asked and making sure the food was great and if we needed more. Cannot keep track how times I have being here on Sundays. Seated right by the front entrance in a 2 person booth.

Still get awesome service at this location.

My husband and I went to Earl's for a late night dinner at the St. Albert location.

The atmosphere was clean and trendy.

After spending 10 minutes deciding on what to order and then ordering... the server then told us they were out of the entree I wanted and the dessert I wanted!

Nothing makes me crazier than deciding on what to order to only then be told that they are out of that item!

We settled on sharing an appetizer of pan bread with balsamic vinegar and oil, a cheeseburger, and sticky toffee pudding for dessert.

It was around 10PM and were were the only table waiting for food. Most of the staff were huddled around the bar area chit chatting.

The meal was pretty good - the prices a little high in my opinion - overall, it was an okay experience - given that the entree and dessert I wanted were "out."

I came to Purple Lotus for the first time today with my fiance. We purchased a Groupon for 2 pedicures and decided to give this place a try after reading some reviews online. 

When we made the appointment we did have to leave a message, but shortly received a call back confirming the time and date that I had requested. 

Our experience was wonderful! It was great to see that they use disposable buckets with a massage chair instead of the jet type massaging chairs; much better for keeping that clean environment. I especially enjoyed the fact that Dallas let me enjoy the pedicure in peace. Some people may prefer constant conversation, but for someone who has to make small talk all day everyday as part of my job, I prefer to just veg out when I am getting a pedicure. The massage portion was great and the paraffin wax very soothing. She did an amazing job and the prices are a little more competitively priced compared to most spas that we go to for the same kind of service. We will definitely be back for more!

Terrible terrible terrible service. I have been to this earls 5-6 times and every time the service is terrible.

The last time was in with a group of 13 people our food came out cold, we had to ask for drink refills and asked 3 times for a desert menu- we were never brought a dessert menu. A friend had to go the front after we sat for 30 minutes with empty glass and dirty dishes in front of us to ask for our bill.

I have been to Connor's 3 times now. Each visit had friendly and interactive staff and service. The layout is the same as the old Beer Hunter; however, the drinks menu and food choices and quality have received a significant upgrade. I may come this Saturday to the Connor MacGregor UFC fight (no cover), as this place is roomy with a few screens. Whiskey Sours-made by Kayla-are supreme! The food is quite good. Bison burgers are top notch taste and quality. Great soup!

Nice pub.  They have a nice patio.  Lots of room inside.  Long bar counter for the regulars. The server with the pink hair was a sweetheart. They have booths.  The staple pub fare was good.  They even have curry if you want that. They have cider too.  There is a stage for music.  Free parking out front. TVs for sports.

I really like Endeavor. I'm glad to see their beers starting to crop up at different places around town. They have a really great brown ale that is a must-try. It's been a while since my visit, so things might have changed since then but I was really impressed with their selection and quality. It's a cool little spot, in an industrial part of St. Albert but it's really nice to see a brewery finding some success out there. They also serve food/bar snacks which I never had the chance to try. I'm really looking forward to my next visit!

First off, as a guy who loves craft beer and incorporates visiting different craft brew pubs during his travels, let me say how excited I am to have a great craft beer spot walking distance from home in St. Albert.

After an apparent delay (some buddies and I showed up the day their website countdown showed them opening only to find them not open for business yet and the countdown clock reset for another two weeks) this great little spot opened in the Campbell Business Park a few weeks back.  After a long day on the football field a friend and I ventured over on their rescheduled opening day for a couple of pints and a growler fill to take home.

This spot is tucked away in behind some other businesses and is not visible from Boudreau Road. But it's well worth searching for. I went back again this past weekend (with my sister this time) again for a couple of pints, a snack and a growler fill.

They have started off brewing only three beers which I think is a smart idea as the three they are doing are great and it is a solid base to work off. I haven't tried the IPA yet (too hoppy is never my thing so I tend to shy away from IPAs) but my football buddy had one and loved it. The Lost Flip Flop Saison is summer in a glass... fruity and crisp and delicious. I myself love the Adventure Brew most and it is what I have taken home with me in my growler both times to be enjoyed in the evening on the back deck.

The room itself is small and cozy, with handmade everything (tables, beer taps, etc) and some board games to keep you busy should you choose. The open concept to the brewery in the back is really cool as well. This place is very unassuming from the outside and it's tinted/ smoked windows. 

I have to add that the food looks awesome and they are providing local choices like Zwicks pretzels and Battistas calzones which is fantastic. But I have to rave about their Salami Chips... thin slices, dried slices of salami with a honey mustard dip. They are very much the perfect snack while consuming beer and have fast become a favourite of mine that I have raved about.

I will hold off on a 5 Star rating until they roll out more beers and maintain the quality of the current line up, which I'm sure they will. The staff here is friendly and welcoming and they have a good thing started that I hope St. Albert supports... I know we will. Great spot and so happy to have these guys in the neighborhood!

-I heard that Earls was having a Patio Party on a Monday night so of course I had to check it out!

Really cool vibe!  Live DJ, corona and Sarac testing and free tacos cooked on the Patio.

 It was a super hot day but most of the Patio was in the shade by 7PM so that was fine.  The Patio is surrounded by greenery and features colorful flowers throughout.

We had tacos, calamari and then a giant peanut butter cookie for desert.  Food was decent.  Staff was very friendly and attentive.  Definitely a fun night on the Patio!

Ambiance: 9/10

Staff and Service: 8/10

Food and Drink: 7/10

Great authentic French Bakery
Best freshlybaked good all the day long.

It doesn't get much better then Endeavor.  I travel extensively and get exposed to many breweries and many types of beer.  Endeavour has the complete package.  Really great beer that is constantly getting better, phenomenal owners that are very family and community oriented, and great staff ( Eric, Jen, Amanda and Stacy) that really go out of their way to service the customers.  If you are in the Edmonton area and enjoy beer, Endeavour should not be missed!

Visited today. Little disappointed in a couple of things. 1) we met friends who got there at 4:50 and ordered drinks from Happy Hour menu. They saw us walk in at 4:58 and asked waitress if we could have our drinks at Happy Hour price as well as we were at our table at 4:59 but she left and didn't come back for 10 minutes so wouldn't let us have ours at HH prices. Whatever, but slightly annoying. 2) I ordered chicken Alfredo, which did not seem to have any kind of Alfredo sauce on it whatsoever. It was more like they doused it in olive oil and butter and threw some Parmesan cheese on it. Totally edible, but definitely not an Alfredo sauce. The other three enjoyed their meals; service was prompt, and, other than the HH issue, the staff were nice. We were asked if we enjoyed our meal by who I assume was the Manager who was also nice. Very pleased to see staff wearing masks as well.

If you are looking for a fun and relaxing patio to dine at this summer I would definitely recommend Earls St. Albert location. 

Stopped in to have lunch with my friend and her aunts. And I have to say it truly was a great lunch. 

I'm not sure if it was the weather and company that made this experience so great but I have nothing to complain about.

We decided to eat outside since the weather was so nice. The patio at the St. Albert location was uber comfortable. With your choice of sun or shaded table. The seats had lots of cushions and tables were decorated with extra throw pillows and even flannel blankets incase you catch a chill from a breeze. I thought that was a really nice touch. The plants and flowers were lush and green.

My friend and I decided to share some appys for lunch. We went with the lettuce wraps, spinach artichoke dip, and truffle fries. The wraps were very flavourful with lots of cilantro and ginger. The truffle fries were pretty unique as well. The fries were on the smaller size. They were soft but not crispy and the truffle aioli that was included for dipping was even better. It seems Earls has really worked to put a unique spin on their dishes and the spinach artichoke dip is no differnt. Again  it really packed a flavour punch and I loved how the artichoke chunks were decently sized. This dish was served with toasted sliced bread. Perhaps my one complaint was that the bread was a bit on the over toasted side making it difficult to bit through because of the thickness of slice. 

The other ladies at the table had order the soup and salad and both were happy with their meal.

Our waitress was very attentive and frequently checked in to see if we needed anything.

This is the most fabulous place for any baking treat in st. albert
I have been there about a dozen times- it is my first choice.  I have also introduced their business to about another dozen friends.
They are friendly, professional and caring. Their coffee is great but you do have to pay for refills.  Their prices are a little high but defintely worth it.
yesterday- my daughter in new york did an on line order for mothers day- she said they were the only bakery in town that offered deliveries. She had no idea that she had picked the winning place but now she knows and so do lots of others. Here is the picture that I sent of the items to lots of people.  The delivery person forgot my strawberry lemondade and the owner Fadoura personally delivered it to  me on her way home after a super busy day- it does not get better than that and that lemoname was the best ever with fresh strawberries in them. I challenge everyone to at least try it- you will wonder why you never did it before.  Lots of people dont know about this place so I hope this review helps.

This use to be the old Beer Hunter but never went there so can't say how much has been changed inside.
We came here on a Wed for half price wings ($6.50).  They were ok, comparable to Brewsters but prefer places that charge 45-49 cents per wing.  I also ordered the calamari ($13.99) and me and my friends were very disappointed in them.  I'd say they were more like fried popcorn pieces with lots of batter, way over fried and I would never guess it was calamari.  Definitely not worth the price and wouldn't recommend them.
The plus side was they have many different beers and the service was awesome.  Maybe will have to try some other items on the menu if ever go back

I love this gym!  After working out at a few other gyms in this area, I can't say enough good things about sturgeon valley athletic club. The atmosphere is calming with low lit lights and no loud music, the amenities are beautifully kept and best of all is the childcare center. My girls (age 4 & 2) love it here!  They ask to go all the time!  No words do it justice...you must see it to believe it. The "jungle gym" makes McDonald's, chuckie cheese, etc look tiny!  And best part?  It's clean!!  Can't say that about those other play places ;). I totally reccomend this gym!!

I purchased a Groupon for pedicure! Dallas did a wonderful job, one of the best pedi's I have had and was treated first class! Was able to get in with in about 2 days and booked online which was easy! 
Only recommendation would be to keep other staff that has nothing to do from gathering at the front desk and gabbing. Not very relaxing. Would go back for a pedi.
This place is so good, the sandwiches are to die for. My new go-to skip the dishes order.

I have been here a couple different times because I really like earls. However, this earls location is by far the worst. Every time I come, the waitress checks on my table a couple times throughout the visit. As well, the waitress takes a long time to come back to bring items such as extra sauces. One time I didn't like my meal  and we were gonna order another item but the waitress never came by. The other person I was out with was half of way done their meal by the time she come by. I didn't want to order because by the time my food would come the person would have to wait. Overall, don't come to this location the service is garbage and they run out of food. The best location is tin palace.

I have to say that I love Earls but will not be returning t the St. Albert one. My sister and I went in on Saturday after choosing Earls to reconnect after 12 years. I walked in and I ordered a 9oz glass of wine with a side car and a glass of ice. The server seemed perturbed that I asked this and said they don't do that, but did come with a side car. My sister ordered a margarita wasn't impressed then ordered a beer. When we were seared there was another customer that was almost in our laps so we were going to change tables but they were all filthy and the server said it was a disaster and they were too busy. She spent most of her time chatting with a men customers. We had to flag her down numerous times for service. It wasn't busy at 2 pm Saturday. As I mentioned this was a reconnect so there were tears on both parts but good ones. We then decided to order food and gobbled it down. It was good. After I had 3 glasses of wine and my sister had a few beers we go to the washroom and the same 3 French fries were still on the floor all mushed. I slipped on them and almost went for a fall, my sister asked the manger to have them cleaned so one falls. The manager (a young 21 yr old) tells her they are busy and we mentioned they have been there since 2 pm, its now 5:15pm. The manager was insulted that a 50yr grown woman is asking to have it cleaned and the manager says she will not be talked to like that. The server then came and asked us to pay the bill as she was going off shift. We paid the bill and then flagged down a server to order another drink as we were wanting another one and waiting for our ride to come have a bite and a drink and then go home. The new server refused to serve us as she said they don't serve mediocre. We then asked for the Manager who sent out the head Chef. He had no clue what we were talking about and then the Manager wouldn't even acknowledge us. 
I have lived in Sherwood Park for the past 10 years and was at the Earls in Sherwood Park roughly 4 days a week. I am on first name basis with all the staff there and have never been treated like this. the lunge in Sherwood Park is exactly that a lounge where children do NOT go. My husband and I were always good for at least $2000 - $3000 dollars a month there.
I WILL DRIVE TO THE SHERWOOD PARK LOCATION ANY DAY OVER ST. ALBERT.
THE STAFF ARE RUDE AND IT IS NOT A CLEAN FRIENDLY ENVIRONMENT...
I like this place. Good beer, patio, lots of seating. Very friendly staff. Easy to get to from Edmonton. We'll be back.

I dropped in a few times. Friendly service, very good food. Ordered wings during happy hour since their website showed them as half price. Raised that with the server. Oh we don't do that anymore. Then take it off of your website. $14 for wings. Not impressed. At least they took it off their website. Should have taken half off the price as well.

When I heard that a Vietnamese fried chicken place was opening, I was all over their social media accounts waiting in anticipation. Owned by the same crew as Jack's Burger Shack and Cerdo Tacos, we're going back to Vietnamese street food here at Ong.

The place itself is small with very few chairs, and a tiny menu. Pretty murals on the walls. Everything is gluten/celiac friendly except for the spring rolls, which are fried in their own separate fryer, so there's no cross contamination. You order at the counter and the food is brought to you/called out by your name.

Spring rolls are reminiscent of home style cooking. Lots of onion, noodles and black mushroom. Comes 5 to an order with a dipping sauce. 

Wings are full wings - not broken apart. So each piece is the tip, drummy and two bone piece. Deep fried and then tossed in a sticky sweet and fish sauce based glaze, then garnished with cilantro. Loved these!

Chicken is a big thigh/drum and a breast piece, both coated in rice flour and fried. Tossed in the same sauce as the wings and served with rice and pickled cucumber. Since the chicken is so much thicker, the flavour of the sauce isn't as pronounced. I like the crispiness and it was very juicy. 

Pro tip: if eating in, there are bottles of sauce on the table that is a lime-y, salty, garlic sauce. Dip your chicken in that and it'll be amazeballs! 

Very excited that this is open and will very happily recommend as an authentic Vietnamese flavour profile. My go-to order would probably be the wings with a side of rice!

I came to Purple Lotus today for the first time.  Their office is located in the Riel Business Park just off the Henday about 5 minutes.

They offer massage, manicures, and pedicures by appointment only.  I enjoyed a 60 minute deep tissue massage by a practicum student who was awesome!  The business owner, Kirsty, greeted me when I came in with a smile.

It's a small little office but they offer a wide array of services from prenatal to deep tissue massages (30-90 minutes), manicures, pedicures, waxing, etc.  Appointment is by booking only and they provide services every day of the week minus Sunday.

And I saw a sign about direct billing, I think it was for Alberta Blue Cross but call them to double check.

They also have a Facebook page and my voicemail to book was returned promptly.
(FB page: https://www.facebook.com/purplelotusmassage)

Cash or Credit or Visa Debit only (no regular interac cards).

Prices were on par with everyone else.

I think another visit will definitely be in my near future...

Service was fast except they never refilled our drinks which is always annoying.  The waiter also dumped our dip upside down on the table and was never cleaned up.  I finally covered it up as it looked like a big bird flew over the table and left us a present, yuck!  Food was good just unfortunate it was not complimented with the refills and cleaning up the mess.  Kind of put a damper on things.

Phenomenal local St. Albert Bistro serving up homemade goodness!  

7-4 M to F and closed weekends.

To die for desserts and made from scratch soups.

I need to come back and try the breakfast wrap!

But today I loved the Brie-lieve it or NOT and the French Onion grilled cheese dip!

Order at the till and they'll bring it to you.

Fast, fresh, and friendly - doesn't get better than that!

I'm not sure if we came on a bad day, but I really didn't think we had a good visit. 

Walking in, there was a really long line of customers. We noticed that they were all standing in front of the Take Out Orders sign, but there were staff with no one in line behind a Eat In Orders sign. We moved over to that person, but were asked to move back into the one line because the computer wasn't working. Moving back, we looked at the menu on the board, but really, aside from the names of the products (and they're cute names, like the Brie-lieve it or not sandwich), there weren't any descriptions. I tried pulling up their online menu and the descriptions were there, so we used that to make our choices.

When we got to the counter, we placed our order - what we both wanted was a sandwich and soup. The staff seemed very surprised since "that's a lot of food; you will probably want the small soup, then." We were told that the hot sandwiches came with potatoes, but we couldn't substitute the soup instead. Ok. So we'll get everything. Paid, took a number and found a seat. 

There are lots of tables and the room is spacious and bright. There's a self serve station for water, which is nice so you don't have to wait. The table next to us were eating a sandwich with a bowl of soup on the same tray - so that made me wonder if we just weren't ordering correctly or if we weren't clear. 

Our soups came out first - $4.50 for a small (which is a good sized bowl) and a cheese biscuit. Tomato basil, it was ok. It wasn't overly basil-y but I threw in a dash of Pepper and it was good. The biscuit was good, though I wish it wasn't so cold.

Our sandwiches came right after - the James Banh Mi ($12) was a letdown. A very soft bun was overfilled with extremely salty shredded pork that tasted like it was soaked in soy sauce. Topped with pickles (on a banh mi? I've never had that before!), sliced jalapenos and a hefty drizzle of wasabi mayo. It was a soggy, overpowering sandwich that I couldn't finish. The Le French Onion Grilled Cheese ($12.25) was beef, onions, mushrooms and cheese on a baguette-type loaf and served with au jus. The sandwich itself was good, but it's definitely more beef dip than grilled cheese if that's what you're craving. The potatoes on the side of both sandwiches were soft and oily, but I do like that they had seasoning and herbs on them. 

A meh experience even though there was such potential.

Had a long wait to be seated which was fine but then had to wait another 30 minutes to get the food.  Our waitress did not actually bring the meals out.  One order was completely wrong and there was no apology.   One plate had food stuck to the bottom which was disgusting.  When it was mentioned all that was said is that they would let the kitchen know.  The actual meals were good but our waitress never came to see how we were nor did she offer drink refills.  For the kids menu they did not have the desert pops that were advertised.  We were told they did not have root beer as they were out.  As result we had some disappointed kids.  When the time to pay came  we were told that only one family could have scene points even though we had 2 separate bills.  The debit system was not working properly and after waiting for over 20 minutes we were finally able to pay.  When we talked to the manager all we got were excuses as to why everything had occurred.  She said they were trying to train the staff and that it was new management and that they were working on fixing the debit machines.  From my point of view I don't care what your challenges are I just want to have an enjoyable meal.  If they had just apologized I would have been happy but this did not happen.  I am really wondering if I will ever go back.

Terrible experience at St.Albert location last night.

Arrived at restaurant at 6.45pm.
- were seated at a DIRTY TABLE that had prior guests dirty food plates, the old napkins and the stained table paper!!!!
- told they were very busy and only table so if we wanted we had to sit and the waitress would clear off
- table was cleared at 7.12PM!!!!!!! We sat at a dirty table for 27 mins and had NO waitress come to clean table, give us menus or take drink orders!!!!
- after asking 3 different servers about getting table cleaned and service, finally girl came and reset table minus cutlery.

- not till 7.40pm did girl come back to take drink and food order!!! Sat for 55mins until we had service!!!

- food arrived at 8.50PM!!!!!!! 1hr and 10 mins after ordering and 2 hrs 5 mins after first sitting down! Was only for table of 3!!!
- when food came all meals were stone cold!!!!!!!!!
Absolutely in edible!!! OH and still NO cutlery!!

Absolute waste of $80!!!!
We asked to speak to manager 3 times by asking 2 different servers and the front greeter person and all said he would come see us.

He NEVER came and so we paid bill and left at 9.30!!

It doesn't matter if restaurant is busy.
It's a restaurant. No excuse for service and food this bad

This is BS!!. I've had to come for test results quite a few times lately and have always had to wait a very long time. Even when it wasn't busy at all. Medicenters need to have a quick access for people who just need results. When I came in this last time all doctors were available and I went right through but am writing this and I've already been here 25 minutes!. This is ridiculous!.

Took in my vehicle for a repair to my heater blower motor. Excellent service and they explained everything clearly but without being condescending. The price was fair and I got my vehicle back quickly. Plus, THEY CLEANED MY CAR!!!! That in itself was worth the cost of my repair! :-)  I will be using these guys in the future!

I came here on Saturday for one of the worst meals I've ever had in my life. The service was awful, it's essentially a bunch of teenager wait staff who are more concerned with texting and hugging each other than doing their job. 

When the food finally came it was cold and just stodgy. I ordered a burger with the sweet potato fries and it was do disappointing. Everything was cold and I found a bunch of random rock hard regular fries in my burger along with a bunch of stale fries onions in my sweet potato fries!! And to top it all off I found someone elses chunk of carrot in my burger!

What my friend got was even worse. Cold chicken, raw vegetables ( like they had literally steamed the veg for probably a min they looked cooked but when you but into them they weren't) and the side of fried mushrooms were completely burnt to a crisp!! There is absolutely nothing reframing about this place.
True Balance did get a hold of me after my review they gave me a credit fr the facial so I book an apt 2 weeks later for botox treatment and it went well.

Nasty nasty nasty! What happened to this place?

Family of four going out for lunch... 

Never ever again to this dump. 


2 minutes from getting in the door we were seated... Good.

10 minutes later we had water.

45 minutes later we had cold raw food with zero sauce on the hamburgers... Just meat and lettuce... COLD RAW Meat.

At this time I also asked for more water and napkins... Never got them.

Went to the bathroom to get a glass of water... Sticky flour and no toilet paper... Gross! 

The only place you have to wash before using the bathroom... Make sure to wipe your feet before getting back into your car... 

Better food and service at 7-11...seriously. 

There for 2.5 hours... The last half hour worn for our $110 bill for shirt food and shirt service..


NEVER AGAIN  !!!



AVOID THIS PLACE UNLESS THEY CLEAN HOUSE.  GET COOKS AND STAFF THAT CARE...
Sandwiches that are both large and delicious. The prices are perhaps a bit high but that's probably just the norm for St. Albert.

I haven't been here in quite awhile. The kids loved in when they were small. Coloring on the table. There's a Balloon man here tonight. Tuesday $4.50 off bottles of wine with your entree. No mozzarella sticks though much to someone's chagrin. They used to be on the menu....All ages can sit in the lounge which we did but sadly discovered that there's no table coloring in the lounge. My steak sandwich was good. The wings were good. Overall good.

Defiantly will NOT come back to this restaurant. 

1# - took 10 min before the waitress came to our table. Didn't even say "hi" or her name. Nothing about specials. Just "can I get you guys something to drink" 

#2 - considering there was only maybe 5-7 other tables being served, we had to wait over 30 min for the food. 

#3 - when food was served, mine was cold chicken and old, cold, hard to chew fries. My husband's fish had raw batter and same kind of fries.

#4 - server had to be flagged down for anything. 

Pretty disappointed in it all. It was my husband's second time here and he did not have very good luck the first time with food. So this is defiantly our last.
Gambling first food and drink second.Always lively.Good live music entertainment weekends.Places are getting a little thin that offer drop in live bar music and dancing.

The last time we were at Montana's was probably 10 years ago and we were not too impressed, however as they had a promotion gong on we went back with another couple.
The "free" appetizer deal card mislead us to believe we could get all three appetizers for free, but to make sure I asked our waitress and she confirmed yes we could get all three free.
Well, low and behold, we were charged for two of the appetizers and when I approached the manager she said there was nothing she could do.  It appears their customer service is still non-existent!  There is absolutely no reason she could not refund the additional charges.

Much to my surprise, the Tudor Glen Medicentre (that has been there my whole life) closed on August 31st and moved to McKenney.

I haven't been to a Medicentre in years, so forgive me if my complaints are just par for the course... but I was really not happy with my visit.

First of all, on a Sunday, there are 2 receptionist working, but only one doctor.  When I checked in, the lady said the wait would not be very long.  She didn't give any specifics - I should have asked.  The wait was 2 hours in the waiting room and then over 20 minutes in the exam room before the doctor came in.  I'm actually not complaining about the wait - It's good to know that the doctor takes his time with the patients.  But there was a serious issue with inconsistent messages coming from the front desk staff.

I sat down, and the next person who came in and went to check in was told the wait would be over an hour.  What?  Is that what we call "not very long"?  okay... weird but whatever, I'm already there.

The next person that came in was told the wait would be 2 hours.

The 10 - 15 people who came in after me were all quoted between 1 and two hours - very inconsistently.  

A lady came in with a UTI (I shouldn't have been able to hear that, but the chairs are set up very closely to the front desk) and when she said she couldn't wait two hours, she was told to come back tomorrow.  

Once I was in the exam room, I noticed two signs on the wall.  They each stated that 2 different doctors will not prescribe T3s, T4s or Tramadol (one will not prescribe any narcotics).  I understand the apprehension of prescribing such medication to patients that you are not familiar with, since this is purely a walk in situation.... but shouldn't those signs be placed in the waiting room?  Imagine waiting 2 plus hours to get in just to find out that the doctor won't prescribe what you're there for.

Anyway.... I'm sure I'll be back since I think this is the only Medicentre in town.  but... meh.

Coming back the Sunday before thanksgiving it was pretty dead so we were all like sweet no waiting. Immediately seated thinking yay starting off good. Went down hill from there. Service sucked, our server seemed more interested in the bigger table where almost everyone was drinking. I never got where people think that they'll probably get a better tip as my boyfriend always is 'give a good tip' since he used to be in the restaurant business.
