I am never disappointed here by the food! The gringo beef tacos are my go to, with a side of rice and beans. The fish tacos are also verrrryy tasty. Don't forget to try a Jarritos while you are there (Mexican soda). I like the lime one.

Two years ago I had another company come to check the furnace before winter, and I got hit with a $75 travel fee, $150 to walk in the door, and got about 20 minutes of their time.   For that we paid over $500 and there was nothing wrong with our furnace.   Wasn't calling them again!   So I looked at reviews, talked to people and True North's name kept coming up with great reviews.   So I called them.   Darryl was the tech's name, and he was here for an hour, checked out everything and found minor problems we should deal with, but nothing major.   The bill was right at $150.   He was efficient, neat, and knowledgable.  I got a call before he came and he was on time.   I couldn't ask for anything more.   I HIGHLY recommend this company.   Thank you, True North!

I've had Cosmic Pizza twice this month after hearing my dental hygienist raved about it! 

So far we've had donair pizza (Amazing) and black olive with feta pizza. 

New pizza and donair shop on the trail across from the Tim Hortons/Wendy combo.

Staff are friendly, pizza made to order in about 10 minutes, and prices fair! 

Two thumbs way up!  Next time, we'll give your donairs a try!

I stopped by here on my way home for the first time today because I didn't have time to cook dinner. My six year old was a little mad because she wanted mcdonald's instead. I let her come in with me and pick the dinner. We got shells filled with sausage and spinach, with a side of cream corn. The owner was working the register and he was very friendly and chatty. You can tell he takes pride in his business. 
When we got home I popped it in the oven and 40 minutes later dinner was served. All my kids enjoyed it, so that's a win in my books. 
It very reasonably priced and I will definitely go back.

Came to the Canadian Brewhouse last month with my son's hockey team for a party.  There were a few hiccups in getting our party booked and then upon arrival the two servers on shift weren't expecting us.

Despite our huge group, we had a great experience!  Sure it took awhile to get our food and they were understaffed (as in one server for our party of 50) but the food was delicious and everyone had a great time. 

The Canadian Brewhouse is a sponsor for St Albert Minor Hockey Association and treated our kiddos to  free pizza and pop as part of our party package.   

We ordered a regular nachos and medium donair pizza and hardly ate half - the portions were huge and the pizza very filling. 

I've previously visited the other St A location for a hockey party and that one had  a few games for kiddos like  foosball and a giant Rubik's cube - I didn't notice anything like that at this location.  Hopefully I just missed it or they will add some :-)

My favorite quick sit down (or take out) restaurant.

Cerdo does a fabulous job of tacos, quesadillas, and huevos. Whether you are in the mood for fish, beef, pork, shrimp, or black beans, they have a tasty dish for you. Gluten free food options abound, due to the corn tortillas, and deft menu design. Friendly staff on top of excellent food. My favorites are the shrimp tacos with an extra half avocado or the fish tacos. For breakfast or brunch the migas bowl. Enjoy!

Richie does my hair satisfied all of the time 
Does great cut n color  never says no when I walk in with no appointment.

Okay, the first time Shawn and I had food from here it was take out, and didn't travel well. I went back recently with my partner, and we both had the gringo beef. It was good, but super super greasy, and nothing to write home about. The service really confused me. Our waitress was super friendly when we got there, and as we sat chatting and such, she kept coming over and telling us there was no rush, all while getting more and more irritated with us. After my partner paid, she slammed the receipt on the table and walked off without a word (and I know the tip was good). This place isn't bad, but the inconsistent service and better tacos elsewhere make me hesitant to come back, even though it's a short drive away.
Awesome atmosphere, great service, large food selection, and drink selection minors allowed till 8pm

Ordered the play maker platter, arrived to pick it up but they didn't see the ticket and didn't make it. They were very apologetic and it took them 15 minutes to make, threw in some extra food and got 30% off the bill. Appreciate the service.

We ordered Cosmic for dinner last week and were pleasantly surprised. The delivery was quick, the food was fresh and the price was about $50 for 3 Large pizzas which is typical. 

I ate the pepperoni pizza with extra pepperoni. It was very flavourful and filling. I've heard raving reviews about this place on local chat groups and had to try. 

Will likely return when I'm looking to switch up my regular pizza order!

We have been going to Famous St Albert for years and we loved it. In the last few months because of Covid 19 we have been ordering with skip the dishes. We have been disapointment with our food. The pizza was always cold and tasteless as well as the salad have very little taste and there was barely any dressing provided. We are so disappointed because it was one of favorite place for pizza.

Pub style food in a very sporty atmosphere. Walls are crammed with all kids of sports and alcohol paraphernalia. When I say crammed I mean crammed there is literally not to many areas where you can actually spot walk.

The location it self is quite large and has a roof top dining area which is probably nice in the summer but not sure how great the view would be since the location is smack dab in the middle of a huge parking lot. Guess I'll have to check it out before judging.

Started lunch out with the CN Caesar. It was so good. My friend is a Caesar making expert and is super picky and she really liked it as well. Canadian brew house has a very large drink menu with tons of cocktails, wine and tap beer. 

For lunch I shared the buffalo chicken poutine and the spinach artichoke dip.
The poutine was not at all what I expected but still pretty good. There were chunks of chicken that had the typical buffalo style sauce on them but that's pretty much were the buffalo flavour ended as well. The gravy was uniquely flavoured with what my friend described as a Cajun flavour. It was oddly addictive.

The spinach artichoke dip was rich and creamy. Unlike a lot of other restaurants there was a ton of artichoke in the dip. When eating with my friend she always orders these types of dips and I think that this place is one of the best of I've had. It wasn't overly salty or spicy. Also included with the usual tortilla chips they also served the dip with little slices of toasted baguette. They were literally tiny pieces of toast to put the cheesy dip on. Yum.

All in all it was a positive experience. The menu is huge so lots more options to explore. They also feature daily specials so I'll definitely be back.

Typical sports type pub, but has a great huge rooftop patio.  Perfect on a beautiful day to chill and have a cold drink.  And as it gets darker and a bit colder they do have huge overhead heaters.  I just had the nachos and they are nice size to share between 3-4 people but gets pricey as you add on beef or chicken and even for guacamole.  Fridays they do have Coors Banquet in tankard size for $7.99.   i don't know if I would come here for a meal, since there are better options out there for price wise, but it seems like a great place to watch some sports or catch up with friends over some drinks.
Great roast beef sandwich dip with tossed salad for the side. Awesome service  once again at Canadian Brewhouse. Just after 11:30am on a Tuesday, not busy

So full disclosure to start with... I so wanted to hate this place. I went in expecting to hate it here, yet I can't. It's a welcome addition to St. Albert.

As a rule I hate chain restaurants and bars and avoid them like the plague. I have always just lumped The Canadian Brewhouse, O2's Taphouse, Browns Social House, First Round, and Hudson's (to name a few) as same sh*t, different pile. These are places I only ever find myself at when invited to a gathering by others... never a spot I would choose to go on my own. Yet I have already been here three times since they have opened...

So why the change of heart? Simply put, this is a pretty damn cool spot with a good beer selection and food that was wayyyyy better than I expected. As well, they have some very cool items decorating this place. Our first venture here was about a week after they opened. Heather and I were caught in the chaos of Christmas shopping and prep and while running to Superstore Liquor she suggested we take a break and grab a drink at the new spot in town next door. We did, and had a couple of fantastic Caesars (we consider ourselves somewhat of Caesar snobs so I think our opinion should be good) and an order of onion rings to nibble on as a snack. So let me say for the record, the onion rings orders here are MASSIVE and they are delicious.  The jalapeno ranch they serve them with is amazing as well.

While on our first visit I learned that they do a FREE Oilers gameday bus from all locations. My previous two visits have been to take in a beer and a bite before heading off to the Oilers game. I have fallen in love with the Tzatziki Greek Wrap (with a side of onion rings of course). There is always a good drink special (Heather took advantage of the Thursday wine specials before a game) and the tankards are awesome. The portions here are sizeable, other people ordering poutine, pizzas and burgers all had amazing looking meals.

The first two times we came here we had a seat at the bar. My only complaint at this place would be that the service at the bar can be a bit dicey. Maybe chalk it up to being a new business but confusion seems to be in abundance when trying to be served at the bar. You never really know who your server is as the lady who introduced herself both times was never seen from again until the bill came. And getting a bill was a challenge both times. The third time we sat at a table and the service was fantastic. We will go that route on future visits.

They have a great looking patio up top that will be a great St. Albert summer addition. I was admittedly wrong on dismissing this spot when I heard it was opening in St. Albert... there's a reason they are a successful chain, they are doing a lot of things right.

Great little vehicle maintenance shop that offers summer/winter tire changeovers for $29.99 - who does that anymore?   The wait here can be long given the excellent price but the service has always been fantastic. 

I'd recommend this shop to anyone looking to save some $$$ on tire changeovers. 

They are located behind Petro Canada on the West side of St. Albert Trail.

Been to Mexico, been to top notch Mexican restaurants. Not really as authentic as I'd like. Good food though. Ok prices. Wasn't really a restaurant for me. I'm used to something else though. I'd recommend them if someone were to ask about them though.

Amore has the best pizza around. The toppings are of great quality, and are plentiful. Bacon, ham and extra cheese is our company favourite. The cheese goes up onto the crust. The staff is friendly, giving a small town feel to a big city pizza parlour.

Just ordered delivery from here. They were out of pizzas, that must mean their pizzas are good. I ordered donators instead. They were excellent. I will definitely order from here next time I am in town.

I have to say this business was outstanding.  We sent an e-mail on Sunday morning, ready to tear out our existing furnace because of non stop issues that no one was able to fix.  Charge us to work on it sure... Fix it not so much.  But True North called us with-in 15 minutes. They sent over a tech, who found 3 separate issues that no one else had noticed, fixed them, and was awesome.  The furnace has worked perfectly... Can not believe the change.  The company called us back 2 days later to ensure everything was going ok... Who does that anymore?
Swift, reliable, well organized... This crew is better than all of the others we had tried combined.
Thanks for the service True North... You are our go-to company from now on.
Rob and Katherine

Nice place in St Albert to go listen to live music.
This night there was a band playing lots of old retro 80's type music.
Laid back type atmosphere, with a nice mix of crowd.
Good service.
Didn't get charged cover this night, so not sure if that's regular thing or not.

Went to get a nail fill , had daughter with me . They asked if I wanted to get her nails done , I said no thanks . They kept pushing. She is 10. 
I said how much ? she said 25! I said sorry that's too much for a kid. She said she will do them for 15 , I said that's ok . She kept insisting, finally I agreed on 15.  Then she said she will also do her feet. I said no , she insisted only 15, to my dismay, I agreed . I said, don't do shellac bc it's too damaging to the nails for a kid. She said she will do only a thin thin layer . 
I go to pay, she said 50 for my 10 year old. I said you said 15 for each . So 30! She said I gave her a manicure . I said I never asked for a manicure !! Or shellac !!!! 
Then she tells me 55 for colour on my nails for fill . I said I usually pay 42-45! 
All in all Michelle has terrible customer service is extremely rude. Argued with me , I will never go back and tell all my friends especially those who live in St. Albert to stay away from this place . I felt sorry for the girls who work under this woman. Also, it's very impolite to speak Chinese in front of your customers . I will report her to the mall.  Stay away !!!! Zero stars !

Yet another pub front that's slowly being run into the ground. The chef quit and he was never replaced, and this shows. The server recommended nachos, maybe that's a sign. The beef dip took a half hour to show up, had almost no beef in it, and was served with a side of potato chips, right out of the bag.  Hope you like sour cream and onion! The wings were OK, good size, nice that they're oven baked. Stick to the wings.

Drinks are watery unless you know someone who knows someone. I asked for top shelf bourbon and got served a lousy sour mash. Sent it back just to get a song and dance from the bartender that he forgot to add bitters, that's why it's so sour. Total BS. The duelling pianos are missing keys. The only thing to recommend this place is a good big screen projection to watch the game.  

The Bourbon Room is on it's way out, not worth stopping by to witness it.

We were anxious to give this new St. Albert business a try this weekend and met friends for an after dinner drink this past weekend. Although billed as a brewing company don't be mislead, they are not brewing beer here as of yet and the information I received is that they hope to venture down that road in 2018. That said all taps were Alberta breweries so that was a plus.

  This was a bizarre experience. They were busy for their first Friday night, and obviously extremely unprepared. We sat with our friends who had arrived before us and already ordered drinks and food (as they hadn't ate yet). Before our waitress came around the couple informed us that the bar "was out of every wine on the menu". Huh? How does that even happen exactly? They list at least a dozen wines on their menu. When our waitress came she confirmed this. I ordered a Fat Unicorn pint and Heather a Moscow Mule. 10 minutes later (5 after my pint was served) the waitress informs Heather they have no ginger beer to make a Mule. Strike two. She then orders a Long Island Iced Tea, which was good.

  Our fiends meals arrived, he had a burger and fries which looked quite run of the mill to me but he said was good. She ordered a kale and quinoa salad, all we could see was romaine lettuce. Again, we didn't actually eat but nothing on our table had visual wow factor.

  Then the most bizarre part happened. Someone kept dimming the lights in the restaurant, then putting them back to bright, then dimming. Repeat this over a one minute span. It was like my 6 year old nephew playing with the dimmer switch in our basement, complete with staff giggling while customers looked around like "WTF?!?". Again, flat out bizarre unless we were missing something completely.

  The couple we were out with are in their mid 60s and she was puzzled that there was no visit to the table from a manager with an explanation or apology about the wine situation. Again everything seemed very disorganized, like they rushed opening this place before they were ready.

  We will give them a few months to work out the kinks and probably see where they are as summer rolls in. Here's hoping it was just opening week issues that are quickly rectified as this is a great location and a cool room with promise.

Gone are the days when Famoso made authentic Italian pizza. The sauce is sugary and in excess, the cheese is barely there, and it's soggy. 

Maybe remove some of your never-ending menu and concentrate on making good pizza again

The rooftop patio is a must for hot summer days! Their Bulldogs are delicious, but they can also just make a classic or flavored Margarita for you! The tacos are delicious and never dry or bland! I highly recommend the Carnitas or Shrimp tacos!

I haven't been to this location in a long time.  I heard The ownership changed (not 100% sure if that's true).  My sister and I were out and about and meeting our mom and her friend for lunch.  We all decided on this location.  

Service was great and food came fast. My mom and I shared a Famouso salad (yum) $15 and a Don Andreas pizza.  My pizza was fairly bland, but I added some red pepper flakes and it was better.  My moms friend had their polenta and a sausage which tasted really good.  I would order that myself.  Great polenta.  

Whether they changed ownership or not it was a successful lunch and I would come back again.

What a cool little store!  My yelping friends have spoken highly of it, so I finally found some time to make it up there.  I actually visited them a couple times leading into the holiday season this year.

They have gifts for everyone and a wide range of prices so they can fit in your budget.  The staff are really friendly and they even offered to gift wrap my purchases even though they were very busy.

The only reason that I had to take away a star was because of all the fragrances in there.  As soon as you open the door, it hits you like a brick wall.  Which leaves me with a headache for my entire visit, and means that my mom cannot even come in with me.  Which is a shame... she'd love it in there!

I've been to many places to get my nails done. Some are okay, usually not close to perfect (a crooked nail here, glue remnants, come off too early...well you know. Then I found Awesome Nails through Yelp. Yes, the reviews are true. The gentleman who did my nails did a fantastic job-acrylic, gel overlay. He is talented and trained in nail art as well. It's been a close to a month, and these babies are holding strong. I need a fill, badly, and will be getting it done here. Hopefully with the same person. It is clean, personable, resonably priced, and the folks are proficient and efficient. The prices are reasonable.

I had Sumono salad and assortment sushi, both were delicious.   The sashimi were fresh which is not common when you have Chinese run Sushi joint.  The waitress were extremely friendly and attentive.  This is authentic Japanese owner/chef which is a huge plus for me when I look for Sushi joint.  I highly recommend this place.

Yuzen ramen is one of the best close to Edmonton. They use to only open Saturday lunch for Ramen but during my visit this week I found out they are open for Ramen Wed- Sun for Ramen. They have a huge selection of different style of ramen, including thin or thick noodles. I got the Traditional Tonkatsu Creamy Pork with side Kara age don. $13 a bowl of ramen is decent price compared to a lot of other ramen restaurants in Edmonton. Broth is perfect and noodle is just the right texture. Highly recommend if you are in the area for lunch!

With my recent pharmacist position transferred to a St. Albert location, I've expanded a lot of my eats to the area. As it's only a 15 minute drive from my house, there really is no excuse to not try restaurants there. Lately, I've had serious cravings for sushi and ever since my trip to LA, I haven't been able to get the same fix. Sushi will never be the same! Good, yes, but not the best I've ever had. There are two sushi restaurants I wanted to try in St. Albert though: Yuzen and Ohana-Ya, both a stones throw away from where I work. First up, Yuzen! (I'll get around to posting Ohana-Ya soon!)

When we came at 6:30pm on a Saturday night, the place was packed! Make sure to reserve a table if you're going during peak hours. The menu has a pretty good selection of appetizers and sushi, less for rolls than most would expect. Priced fairly reasonably as well!

First order was the tuna tataki, seared and in a garlic soy sauce. The sear was a bit much for me, cooking more of the tuna that I would have liked, but if it weren't so, it would just be straight up sashimi in a sauce. I'd almost prefer it as such, but that would make me a fool for ordering tataki and expecting something else. The garlic soy sauce was nice and light, making the dish easy to eat. Most importantly, the tuna tasted super fresh!

To compare my favorite type of roll, I ordered the spicy tuna. I ordered it with tobiko (flying fish roe) but it can be ordered with plain sesame at a cheaper price. The tuna was spicy, but my favorite is still Kyoto and Ichiban's spicy tuna maki. Something about the smaller maki makes the proportions of rice to fish ratio that much more appealing. This was still good though!

Joe ordered the assorted sushi combo, coming with 7 pieces of nigiri (including a tamago sushi), and one salmon hosomaki (the equivalent of the smaller maki rolls at Kyoto or Ichiban). This was probably the best deal yet, at $18 for the combo, fairly large portions of nigiri, and fresh sashimi to boot. To date, this is as close as I have gotten in Edmonton and area to my sushi experience in LA. Very nicely done! Watch out though, done to true fashion, there is a bit of a wasabi rub in between the sashimi and the rice.

Not quite so full yet, we also ordered the mozuku, a string seaweed, marinated in a vinaigrette dressing. I was expecting a seaweed salad, something with crunchier texture that was marinated differently, but instead I got a very stringy, soup-like bowl of seaweed. The agar of the seaweed seemed to be extracted out by the vinaigrette, making the soup fairly slippery and slimy! The taste was good, but the texture wasn't a hit for me.

For dessert, three matcha ice cream mochi balls for us. Although not handmade (anybody know of a place in Edmonton that does?), and imported through a supplier, it was still a great dessert. The outer rice cake layer was done thinly (my preference), and the ice cream rich in flavor. Yum!

Since opening a little over a year ago, Yuzen hasn't reached to my ears by many sources. Hopefully you guys check it out next time you're craving for a sushi place! When I posted a photo on Instagram (follow me for sneak peaks at my upcoming posts), there was a comment that I should try Ohana-Ya. Mind reader! That post is to come so check out which one I thought was better! There was also a couple of comments that the service was slow. I thought our server did a great job getting our orders and our dishes and with one sushi chef plain in sight for you to see, I don't blame the ever so slightly slower prep. He's cutting fish, I'd rather he do it right!
Amazing food, wonderful presentation. I've eaten here many times and have always had a good experience. When it is busy they can suffer from a lack of serving staff.
Poorly stalked shelves make me cry. The clerk yelled at me for paying with cash and the door was broken.

April 2014 update 

I originally rated this place 4 stars per info below. The last few months it has gone down hill big time. I have tried talking to the owner a few times but it does not seem to make a difference. It really is too bad because this place was very close to home.

Old 4 Star Rating comments from pre Jan 2014

Along with Thanh Thanh downtown, this is one of y two favourite Vietnamese style restaurants in the Edmonton area so far. Very good variety on the menu from traditional Vietnamese to more fusion dishes and a good selection of spicy dishes as well. A little pricey for this type of restaurant but given the food quality I am willing to pay the higher price.

Very few Asian restaurants have truly outstanding service so by Asian service standards this is is actually pretty good. Always friendly fairly fast etc. In Vietnam it is considered rude to bring the bill before it is actually asked for. Remember this or you could be sitting a long time after supper.

The one downer, we had reservations to meet friends there on Aug 4th, only to arrive and find a sign saying closed Aug 4th and 5th (which is the long weekend). Don't know if an emergency popped up but I will definitely mention it the next time we are in as it is pretty annoying.
Excellent sushi and customer service! Also has gluten free soy sauce and menu items if you ask :)

Apparently, this restaurant has been opened as early as 2011, but it's a wonder how this gem stayed hidden! I had recently heard of this place and my friends were saying that it was hands-down the best ramen in town. Now don't be fooled...it is NOT a ramen restaurant. Disappointing...as they only serve ramen on Saturday mornings (11:30am to 2:00pm), but if you like ramen, you have got to give this place a try!

The portion is a little small compared to other ramen places in the Greater Edmonton Area and the price tag is the same at around $12. Taste-wise, it is the most flavourful broth currently available here. When you order, there are add-ons and I highly recommend adding the egg to your order. Those who don't like their eggs runny should skip this option. For those that love their meat, be warned that a bowl only comes with 1 slice of cha shu (pork), so adding meat may be something you would want to consider.

The noodles are cooked well and are slightly chewy, which is how I love it. One disappointing fact is that the noodles are not handmade by the restaurant. Traditional ramen is supposed to be handmade and paired with a rich pork broth. A plus is that this Japanese restaurant is actually owned by Japanese person, complete with a fluent, English-speaking Japanese waiter. While that doesn't guarantee authenticity or quality, Japanese foodies would know that is a rare occurrence now as most Japanese restaurants are Chinese owned/run.

Oh, I almost forgot to mention the delicious dessert. While most Japanese restaurants serve ice cream mochi, these were the best I have ever had! The rice dough outside layer was very thin and evenly distributed. They allow you to order any mix of flavours within an order. At $5 for 3 mochi, we ordered two orders (two of each flavour - chocolate, black sesame, and green tea). We were still contemplating how to split 6 mochi among 4 people as the order arrived. They had cut them into 12 perfect halves, ready for sharing. Talk about service! The ice cream was creamy smooth inside and were not at all runny from being cut open before serving. Also, the shape of them looks like they had been popped out of a mini muffin tray, which leads me to wonder if they had made it themselves.

All in all, I will definitely be paying Yuzen another visit sometime soon - both for their ramen and to try out the rest of their menu.

Nail places are a dime a dozen in some spots, but I'd head into this one again! Awesome Nails just opened in St Albert last December. I phoned in on Sunday asking if they took walk ins, which they totally do and found myself promptly seated when I walked through the door at 2pm.

The salon itself is pretty big and very clean. There are half a dozen foot bath chairs for pedis and a similar amount of manicure stations. They are also equipped with everything you'd need to get whatever body part waxed.

I needed a manicure in a bad way. My nails haven't seen a salon since, well longer than I'd care to admit. My mani included the usual nail clean and care, some pretty pink gel nail polish and a nice little hand and arm massage at the end. I was in and out in just over 30 minutes and all for under $35. 

If I find myself in St Albert needing a manicure again, I'd totally come back!

I went to this nail spot because of the great reviews. I was not disappointed they were awesome!!! I had a pedicure and manicure and was in and out in an hour. Super friendly and accommodating. I highly recommend this place!!

Great little Japanese restaurant in St. Albert.  Been here for dinner and for the Ramen on Saturdays ( Lunch time )
Dinner : 
Crispy Cajun Roll - a unique take on a roll but really tasty, comes with a spicy Cajun mayo, Excellent
Black Cod - teriyaki style was very good.  Fresh fish and fish only, so you need to add rice if needed.
Yakisoba - good fried noodle dish if you want something different than teriyaki or rolls/sushi
Sushi/Rolls - fresh fish.  Had really good, fresh Uni there when I was there.  Nice California rolls.  Spicy tuna was ok.
Mochi - green tea, good 
Saturday Ramen :
I love their Ramen ( love meaning almost every Saturday ).  The two I alternate is the Tonkatsu ( pork ) and Tan Tan ( spicy pork ).  I always add 2 eggs to the soups, just perfectly cooked eggs that create a nice creaminess to the soup when opened.  My comparison is to Monta Ramen in Las Vegas and this place is right up there.  Prices are more here but anything off strip in LV is pretty cheap.

I heart Yuzen.

I've only visited a handful of times due to my children not really being sushi kind of kiddos but man have our meals here been excellent!

Highlights for me included the red bean mochi - how on earth can a red bean dessert be so delicious?  I don't know how, but it was!

On our last visit, hubby and I enjoyed 4 appetizers, one tempura udon dish, and 3 mochi to split. 

From the service to food, it just could not have been done any better.

Thank you YUZEN for being delicious!

I MUST must MUST come try your Saturday AM ramen!

The name really does say it all, this place is awesome.  They take the time to do an incredible job every time I go and make sure you are 100% happy before you leave. With a Manicure and pedicure they give you a nice massage and as an added bonus a hot towel on your legs and arms.  They remember every colour I have ever tried and the ones my friend and sister get.  They also remembered our names after the first time we went.  Excellent place to get your nails done with the most incredible owners!

I booked an appointment for a contact lens fitting and was quoted $40 on the phone. When I arrived to my appointment, the receptionist informed me that they could not give me contact lenses unless I had an eye exam as well. But, I had just had an eye exam one month ago at a different optometrist, which I  did bring the prescription along with me.  The receptionist said they needed my file faxed over from where I had my eyes tested, but had no luck in receiving it. 

I expressed my concerns that I was unaware of this when I booked the appointment and felt it was a mix up on their part. The receptionist apologized for the mix up. 

I asked the receptionist if they are willing to do my eye exam but waive the fee. She kept repeating that its the optometrist's 'license on the line'.  I work as a registered nurse and fully understand this; but as a client I was not informed of what paperwork was needed for this appointment. I don't ask for things often, but I thought to suggest if the eye exam could still be done. The receptionist responded 'we can't just give you a free eye exam!'. In the end, I just chose to leave. 

I was not asking for something for 'free'.  I just felt that if a company and service provider made a mistake, that they would be willing to accommodate for their clients. They look like a well established company but after this experience my perception upon leaving was that they just care about making money and not taking care of their clients. 

 Initially, I chose MDO since I was a client there years ago and they were great. After this, I don't think I will return.

It's unfortunate that they only serve ramen on Saturday.  It was delicious though, and worth the trip to St. Albert. One thing that bothered me was how excessively thirsty I was for the next 12 hours after eating there.  I knocked off one star because of too much of whatever it was that made me thirsty. (I fear msg cause regular salt doesn't do that, but I don't want to say for sure because I don't totally know) If I could do half stars,  if also dock half a star because the staffing seems to be under-manned on Saturday, and a little green.  I've been there during the week and service is better.
Probably the prettiest flower design I've ever had on my toes :) Super good job at a really reasonable let price!

Authentic and delicious.

 Yuzen is run by a real Japanese sushi chef. He was trained in Japan and the sushi cuts and food flavour reflects his expertise.

I grew up around Japanese people and real Japanese food. Yuzen is serving the real thing.

This is the kind of hole in the wall place that survives on quality not show. The service is OK and the decor is too but none of that matters once you get started on the food.

This is a limited review, as I specifically went there for a single dish; the ramen. I went it with a bit of trepidation, as I've had ramen from other restaurants recommended to me before, and it's always been a disappointment. Not so with Yuzen, it was delicious and well worth the trip. Excellent quality ingredients, fresh and clean and....well, to make a long story short, this is the place I'll come to for ramen in Edmonton. I hope the rest of their menu is as tasty, and I also hope they'll start serving the ramen more often, I usually prefer to sleep in on Saturday mornings  :)

I recently moved to North Edmonton and was craving a bowl of ramen - St Albert is a short drive away, so away we went. I've had ramen throughout Singapore and Vancouver and I wouldn't say I'm picky, but I do know that the broth is a huge component of your ramen experience.

I would say first of all, that the best part of Yuzen is their noodle. You can order thick or thin noodle - I ordered the thick noodle and was not disappointed - it was beautifully textured, fresh tasting and had just the right amount of chew. I'm a fan based off their noodles alone. The pricing is comparable to any other ramen joint you might visit and the serving side is generous.

The broth in the ramen is A-OK, nothing terrible but I did suspect that they didn't spend 18+ hours making their broth like some other restaurants do. I had the tonkotsu, which is my favorite soup wherever I go, and while it was rich and creamy, it was missing that little bit of color and depth that other soups have offered.

The pork char siu was very tender - the cut they offer is like a "roll" rather than basic slices, so it does have a different texture but isn't terrible. The longer you leave your pork in the soup, the more tender and better it tastes!

The service was very attentive and our meals arrived quickly. Overall, I wouldn't hesitate to come back, however this isn't my go-to spot when I'm wanting a real A+ quality broth! However, best noodles in Edmonton. Thank you, Yuzen.

Shut. The. Front. Door.

If this isn't the cutest gift shop ever?!?

There seriously isn't a person in my life that I couldn't buy something for here.

And they do complimentary gift wrapping!

And there are some serious cool local items - like lip balm made from St. Albert Bees!!! Well, not the bee itself but you get my drift!

This place is by far the best nail salon I have ever been to. Service is exceptional and I've never been happier with my nails. Vinh, the salon's owner, is very meticulous and that's what I love about his work. He's very precise in every step of the process ensuring every nail is perfect (& they are!) This does mean that he takes a little longer with them but I would much rather have high quality nails than a quick but substandard job. I usually get gel nails done and they've never chipped or broken off - my nails feel so durable that even when they've grown out a lot I'm not scared that they'll break. The quality of the service is so good that it makes driving out to St. Albert so worth it (I live in Edmonton). I would highly recommend this place to anyone with zero hesitation.

3 girlfriends and I came in for pedis and ended up with manis as well! Fantastic service and super accommodating staff, one girl called in sick so it was just two of them and they did everything they could to not have us waiting. Will definitely be back!! Fantastic day!

First time here. Authentic Japanese ramen noodle house owned by Japanese people. Totally legit and delicious!! Price is reasonable. Noodles and soup all very delicious!! Also had beef tataki as a starter and was tasty as well, and only $10.50!! Would recommend!!
The Ramen is so delicious! Great lunch spot! I order the spicy miso ramen with an egg. Warms you up on a cold and snowy day. Service is great and fast.

My husband & I went to the Asian Banana Leaf for the first time & we loved it!  The menu selection is fantastic.  What to order???  So much choice.

We ordered the smaller sized bowls of Wonton Soup & the Coconut Milk Soup with Chicken.  As you can see from the pics, the portions were huge!  And absolutely delish.  This was accompanied by a Spring Rolls appie.   For our main meals, we ordered the Pork & Prawn Cucumber Salad & the Pad Thai.

Honestly, everything was so, so good.  No complaints at all.  The service was excellent (however, at that time, it was virtually empty...)

The previous complaints abut the music must have been rectified because I believe there was music playing in the background, but at a very low volume.

We were so impressed with this find & we can't wait to go back to sample other choices on the very impressive menu.

My new favourite nail salon! My mom and I decided to get pedicures this afternoon, and I had been told this was the place to go. Firstly there was no overpowering chemical smell like most nails salons, and secondly - the customer service was unreal! We had appointments and were greeted with smiles and quick service right away. We had lots of colours to choose from and both of our pedicures turned out awesome! A very clean nail salon and inviting atmosphere.
Decent location, then I saw Sam B. And ran as fast as I could. I went there the next day and the building was not under lockdown, wth.

Both the service of the staff and the quality of the eyewear at MDO are unbeatable.

When you enter the store, you're greeted by a friendly, smiling face and immediately invited to sit down. You have a chat with the staff member taking care of you to help them understand what you're looking for, e.g. "I want to add some colour to my eyewear collection", "I want a classic frame that can go with anything", "I'd like something with a funky shape", etc. The associate will assess your face to determine what sort of frame will fit you best (personally my face is kind of small, and the bridge of my nose particularly small, which really impacts the fit of various frames), then bring you a tray of frames to try on. 

There's none of this wandering around a crowded store asking to see this and that pair, only to try them on and see that they are completely unflattering. Usually, if my eyewear consultant at MDO doesn't like a frame on me, I don't even bother looking in the mirror (I learned after my first few visits that they're going to be right anyhow). My glasses have always been ready within a few days (I've even had them done same day while I wait when the lenses are in stock). I look forward to shopping here for a long time to come!
Great Nail Salon! It's clean, service is reasonably priced and staff are knowledgeable. So happy to find this gem, will definitely go back!!

Pricy but aside from that they had great food, good selection of Asian beers, quick service, and even the bathrooms were very nice. I will admit, that another review posted, that the music selection was odd. They were playing western classical music and it didn't seem to fit the setting of the restaurant at all.
The ramen here is 10/10. The spicy tan tan is so delicious, my husband and I can't stop thinking about it. If you like ramen, this is the place to go. The drive is totally worth it from Edmonton.
This restaurant was my absolute favourite! I hope the open again! Even if its a food truck! Soooooo goood! Have yet to find anything to compare

Yuzen's rebranded to what they're now calling Menya Yuzen. With that comes a brand new menu and a ramen only joint. That's right, you read right, they only serve ramen. They've opened up a sushi shop in St. Albert, Sushi Yuzen (585 St. Albert Trail). 

We came on a late Saturday (1:00pm) as I was hoping to miss the first rush but it was packed. I put our name down and were quoted 45 minutes. Turned out to only be about 20-25 minutes. Not too bad.

The menu has appetizers, sashimi, donburi and traditional/gyokai tonkotsu/tonkotsu mix/spicy ramen options. 14 varieties to choose from. Curious if the abura soba (soupless) is good.
 
- Seaweed salad ($3.50) - this came with their lunch special. Good but a bigger portion would have been appreciated. 
- Tako-wasa ($4.50) - I'm not a huge tako fan but the raw marinated octopus was done well. The wasabi is very prominent. 
- Gyokai tonkotsu ($13.50) - this is their new broth! A mix of traditional, pork and seafood. You can really taste the funkiness of the seafood. Delicious. I'd asked for the thick noodles but they messed up and brought me thin ones. No worries, they still had a great, chewy bite. We asked for the noodles to be a bit harder/al dente which they nailed. 
- Traditional tonkotsu ($13.00) - CC added an egg ($1.00) to her bowl. The tonkotsu itself is creamy and rich. Love this one as well. 
- Shoyu tonkotsu mix ($13.00) - J also added an egg. Their egg can use some work. The broth was much lighter and cleaner than the other two. 

I barely go out for ramen in Edmonton because the scene is awful but Menya Yuzen is the only place I'll make an exception. 100% worth the drive!

Being a new resident of St. Albert, it's hard to find an authentic, down to earth, good quality Japanese fare, but Yuzen always hits the spot!

Pro:
- Authentic, Japanese owned establishment
- They always have awesome and unique specials, like monkfish liver, tako wasa, yukke, etc. Stuff that you can't find in many other Japanese restaurants
- The ramen specials on Saturdays. 

Cons:
- There isn't much of an atmosphere
- It's pricy

Ended up here almost by accident a few weeks ago...one of those spots we see often and always say "we have to try that sometime" but had never made it to until recently. We were missing out.

We were grabbing our booze for May Long at Ace Liquor (same parking lot) and hadn't ate dinner yet. Heather asked if I wanted to keep it simple and go for a bowl of ramen at Yuzen so we decided to finally give it a shot.

We started with the Bean Sprout Salad which was fantastic. To be honest I don't even remember which ramen each of us ordered... Heather went with a creamy broth and I went with a clear, spicy broth. Both were fantastic and mine was spicy hot to the perfect level. The noodles and toppings were fresh and delicious. We left full and happy and will return soon when the urge for ramen returns!

Service was excellent and the restaurant was small, very clean and somewhat ordinary but nice!

The staff at Awesome Nails did a great job on my shellac manicure/pedicure. I had two nail technicians working on my hands/feet, so they got me out of there quickly. The polish was applied well and lasted through my whole vacation. There were many colors to choose from. I also enjoyed the massage chair. Thank you!!

I took my wife here on a lunch date on the recommendation of a friend. I have to say that I was extremely happy with the ramen and the service. The restaurant was full but not crowded. The server checked on us the proper amount. The food was fantastic. I will definitely be returning often

Yuzen only serves ramen on Saturdays from 11:30-2:00 PM. We arrived at about 11:50 to find the restaurant packed with hungry patrons, and we were quoted a 15-20 minute wait time. The restaurant can accommodate about 40 people including the seats at the bar, but the space is pretty small so you wait outside of the restaurant until your name is called. Service seemed to be pretty quick because it felt like we were seated in no time. 

The Saturday lunch menu features five different bowls of ramen (shoyu, shio, tonkotsu, miso, tan tan men), optional extra toppings, and a few sides like gyoza (panfried pork dumplings), ebi shumai (steamed shrimp dumplings), and rice bowls. All the ramen bowls come with the standard char siu, green onion, bamboo shoots, and roasted nori sheet, unless otherwise specified. My boyfriend ordered the Tonkotsu ramen ($11), which was garnished with wakame and beni shoga in addition to the regular toppings. One look at the broth and I was excited - the cloudy soup hinted at signs of a rich, flavourful broth, and that's exactly what we received. Thick and creamy, the broth gave a flavourful punch with each bite into the al dente noodles. The char siu was quite fatty, but was moist and flavourful, making this a pretty good bowl of ramen. My boyfriend actually found the broth to be a little too rich for his liking, but I would have happily devoured the entire bowl. 

For myself I had the Miso ramen ($11) which was served with bean sprouts, spicy ground pork, green onion, bamboo shoots, and the roasted nori sheet. The ground pork was in place of the char siu, so I ordered a side of char siu (5 pc, $2.50) to come with my noodles. The miso broth was not quite as thick as the Tonkotsu, but it had depth and a strong miso flavour with a bit of heat. The noodles had a nice bite that lasted to the end of the bowl, and it was a filling, hearty bowl of noodle soup. 

Yuzen does a great job with their broth for ramen, making it in house on Friday nights to prepare for the Saturday rush. Like other Japanese restaurants with ramen on their menu, Yuzen brings in the noodles from a supplier here in Edmonton. Makes me wonder when we will have a dedicated ramen restaurant that makes both their broth and noodles in house! Speculation aside, the bowls of ramen were awesome for Edmonton standards and are comparable in price to other restaurants. The broth was flavourful and the noodles were cooked well, so I would definitely return in the future. If you're in the area on a Saturday afternoon or are willing to make the trek for some ramen, try out their bowls!

If there was a 2.5 rating I'd give that, but I just CANNOT round up to 3 stars for this dining experience.

I brought my mother and daughter today to celebrate her first school concert - Proud Beaming Mama - she did great :-)

But... lunch was not so great.

Asian Banana Leaf is a new "Vietnamese and Thai" restaurant in St. Albert which has opened up in the place of the now defunct Indian Restaurant, The Copper Grain.

The inside is still beautiful and the atmosphere is inviting and spacious but that is where the good stuff ends.

I visited the washroom which was clean but pitch black and no light switch could be found inside.  I had to elicit the help of staff to use their magickal powers to enlighten the washroom ( I think the switch is probably on a main panel).

We decided to order the Appetizer sampler for $22.99 which listed: spring rolls, salad rolls, deep fried wontons, fried squid, green onion cake, and fried shrimp.

Upon arrival - it was missing the salad rolls altogether and something had been substituted for the "fried squid."  I waited for the waitress to return but she did not.  Finally, I got up and grabbed a menu to review the description and walked over to the doors to the kitchen to signal for staff.

When the waitress came out she did not apologize and did not offer to rectify the situation.  Instead, I had to convince her to come over to our table (and we were the ONLY table in the restaurant at 1115am) to review what we had received.  Eventually she said she would ask if they could make the salad rolls.  With regards to the deep fried squid, she said that the little balls on our plate were kind of like fish cakes but made with mixed pork and squid.  I have had them before on vermicelli bowls and a fast one was not about to be pulled on me... It was anything but "fried squid."

Anyhoo... The items were all overcooked unfortunately, the spring rolls were more like crunchy rolls according to my Mom - she didn't even though my toddler would be able to bite through the ends.  My daughter ate most of the green onion cake but even that was overly crunchy.  The pork/squid hockey pucks were greasy and sweet.  When the salad rolls did arrive, they were smaller than your average salad rolls and did not contain any basil or garnishes - only pork, shrimp, lettuce, and noodles.  The accompanying peanut sauce was pretty good.

For whatever reason, only two water glasses were brought to our table for 3.  And even though we were the only customers in the entire restaurant, at no point in time did our waitress check in with us.  I had to go to the kitchen to address the mistakes and find her for more water.

My Mom ordered lemongrass beef on vermicelli and I ordered grilled beef and shrimp on vermicelli - both were $12.99.

The vermicelli bowls were okay - nothing to write home about.  The beef was okay, but definitely not tender.  My shrimp were fair but slightly overcooked.

The fish sauce was fair - although, again, I prefer a more seasoned fish sauce.  On the table was one kind of hot sauce which helped spice up our meal.

Our bill came to just shy of $50 when the 15% grand opening discount was applied (this discount runs through the first week of January 2013 if you'd like to give them a try... )

I had inquired if they made Pad See Ew (my husband's favorite Thai noodle dish, and the waitress' response was one of confusion and she suggested I try Pad Thai...)

I don't think we will return... All of the Thai dishes which appealed to me were in the $18 price range and that's just too steep for my blood for a quick lunch time bite.

I like this place :) pretty relaxing, good choice of selection; their rolls, satay, and wonton appetizers are good. Their coconut rice is unsweetened (it tends to vary with thai restaurants) but they provide 'soy ketchup' (like thick, sweet soy sauce) as a condiment, which is my favorite.

I crave their peaches and cream chicken now and then, and anything with lemongrass on the menu is a safe bet :) especially the shrimp on sugarcane. If you've never had a sugarcane skewer I highly recommend it.

It's a nice place to go with friends as it is usually quiet. My only complaints are that sometimes the music is repetative (as others have said) and the restaurant can be quite cold at times (too much air conditioning). Other than that, it's a nice place to check out if you want vietnemese but don't want to drive too far.
Best place for a pedicure!   Friendly staff,  great hours, convenient location and my toes look beautiful for a very  long time!   Highly recommended!
Fantastic sushi.  Great service! Parking is a bit difficult but not terrible to manage.

3 Visits, 2 remakes of glasses I had to pay for and still could not see well. Poor distance vision, double vision headaches and more. Went and had my eyes re-examined at Sturgeon Vision Centre, TOTALLY different prescription, but back a lot closer to the original prescription I had before I moved to St Albert. I can now see 20/20 again.

Weekends are for ramen and weekends are why we drive out here. Saturday and Sunday, they only serve a limited menu and it's only ramen. There's always a line, so you put your name on the list and wait or leave your number and they call you about 5 mins before - though they've added hours (used to only be Saturday lunch, now it's all day, all weekend). They're not a huge space, so they do a communal table for smaller parties to get more people in - if you have an aversion to sitting with people you don't know, be aware of this.

The ramen is good - about $13 on average and you can add a bunch of toppings for extra charges. The portion is decent, though a bit smaller than some other places. All the broths are delicious - there really isn't an option I have tried and didn't like. I love the noodles. Such a good texture and bite to them.

Definitely recommend!!

Yuzen. If you don't already know, they serve ramen but only on Saturdays. I tried going recently and it's PACKED. If you're planning to go, get there early. By early, I mean before they open (11:30am) otherwise be prepared to queue in line.

The interior is small with only room for maybe 20 customers or so. Hence why it's packed for ramen. You could call it cozy and intimate but the décor is pretty minimalist.

- Miso soup - they always start your meal off with a miso soup that is light and not too salty.
- Matsu bento box ($15.00) - six pieces of sashimi, three nigiri and three sashimi maki rolls. Comes with salad and a side bowl of rice. I've had this twice now and while it looks small compared to the ume bento, there is a lot of food. The salad has a sweet, tangy vinaigrette. The sashimi/nigiri is pretty standard (salmon, tuna and shrimp). I wish they gave a better variety of fish though. For the price, it's quite reasonable.
- Ume bento box ($12.00) - my buddy is a little less adventurous when it comes to sushi so he always sticks with the safe bento boxes. Comes with rice, salad, tempura, California rolls and your choice of teriyaki chicken or yakiniku beef. He went with the former.

Things are a little more pricey at Yuzen for dinner but I've only ever been during lunch times. The bento boxes are good value if you want to try a bit of everything. Great spot to grab some quality Japanese food.

Pro: great food! Pho broth is full of flavor, huge portions and friendly service. 

Cons: service is slow and they have to stop playing the same music over and over again.
The packed deli meats are well-arranged and laid out., making it super easy to pickup and go. I have seen a fly inside their pastry counter, so I avoid in-store sweets.

This is by far the BEST nail salon in St. Albert. Trust me - I've been to many of the others, and they all pale in comparison.  Everything is AWESOME at this salon.  The salon is always so clean and everyone that works there is so friendly. Cam does a fantastic job, and he is amazing with his free hand designs. My nails actually last between appointments. At all the other places, my nails look like crap 3-4 weeks later as they always break and chip - but at Awesome Nails, they still look exactly the same (except for my nails have grown out of course!). I wouldn't go anywhere else - so grateful that Awesome Nails has opened in St. Albert!!

I have been craving ramen for quite some time now. Man, I wish Edmonton was more like Vancouver/Toronto/Montreal/even Calgary...alas, what can you do. I've actually heard about Yuzen several times from co-workers and friends and coincidentally, it is right by the barbershop that I frequent (shout out to Barbershopboyz - it's tough to find a good barber, you're welcome). Anyways, this review is only for their ramen as we went on a nice, sunny Saturday afternoon.

I like places that specialize on doing a few things well and only focusing on ramen is a good sign.

We tried two different types of ramen:
 - I had the miso ramen ($11): it came with ground pork and bean sprouts.  It was decent but I wasn't blown away by the flavours. The noodles had a nice firm, chewy texture to it but it's not homemade (if you are a purist). It has a "spicy" sign beside it but I didn't taste any spiciness to it.

- My dad and friend had the tonkatsu ($11 + $1 egg). My friend thoroughly enjoyed it and same with my dad, except he thought it was a bit on the salty side. I will have to try this one next time as I am more of a fan of tonkatsu (but wanted to order something different).

Anyways, as I said before, ramen places are a dime a dozen in this town, especially good ones. Yuzen is your best bet to get your ramen fix. That being said, I've heard nothing but great things about their sushi so I will have to check them out for sushi sometime soon hopefully!

Last Saturday, I dragged Sharon up at the crack of dawn (that's 11am people) to Yuzen in St. Albert for their Saturday-only ramen. Ramen is one of my all time favorite foods. It's a shame that, at the time of writing, I only have one post tagged as ramen. Edmonton just doesn't have a lot of options! And although we have no designated ramen houses, we do have Japanese restaurants that serve ramen. Most notable is Nomiya's ramen on Calgary Trail, a go-to place for Joe and I when we're craving noodles other than pho or bun bo hue. So when word started spreading that Yuzen's ramen was better than Nomiya's... well you know what happens next.

Most important to note, the restaurant doesn't open until 11:30am. So although I told Sharon we needed to be up and at 'em for 11am, we ended up patiently waiting in the parking lot for the that signage to light up with the beautiful words, "open". We weren't the only ones. Our car neighbors, also of the Asian sorts, were also waiting for this once a week ramen. That's a good sign? I wonder how far they traveled! Saturday lunch at Yuzen is ramen only! No sushi orders and no other menus aside from their ramen menu.

I was expecting only one style of ramen, so it was a surprise when five options were available. That's like a full ramen house! Nice to see the traditional four broths plus a Tantan-men. All bowls are served with cha-siu (sliced BBQ pork), menma (bamboo shoots), negi (green onion), nori (dried seaweed) unless otherwise stated. Extra toppings could also be added on and if a bowl of soupy noodle goodness just didn't cut it for you, traditional sides are available, such as: gyoza (Japanese pork dumplings), ebi shumai (shrimp dumplings), rice bowls, or fried rice.

Sharon initially wanted to order the Tantan Men, a sesame paste based broth that's actually a Chinese dish (also known as dan dan noodles). I've had some experience with tantan ramen before and it is just not my style. Rich in flavor, creamy, thicker sesame-based broth, and sometimes with a hint of peanut sauce, I find it overpowering and hard to finish a whole bowl. Don't get me wrong, it's delicious. But not what I think of when ramen comes to mind. Having expressed my opinions, Sharon ordered the Tonkotsu, a pork bone broth. Her bowl came out as a thickly clouded white broth, creamy, and traditional of that style. That's what happens when bones, fats, and collagen are boiled over a long period of time! The standard toppings completed her dish, creating a homecooked meal look. Sharon enjoyed it although couldn't compare it to Nomiya's, believing that either would be good and you'd have to do a side by side comparison to really point out a winner.

I decided to order my standard fare that I usually get at Nomiya, a spicy miso. Miso broths use a ton of miso paste and blended into chicken or fish stock, and even sometimes crossed over with Tonkotsu broth. The result is a slightly sweeter, nuttier? flavor, and not quite as thick as the Tonkotsu or Tantan-men. Instead of cha-shu, my bowl came with ground pork and beansprouts. If you know me at all, you know I cannot eat ramen without a soft-boiled egg.

A ajitsuke tamago, a soft-boiled marinated egg, is what makes a ramen dish complete to me. Without it, I'd have to deduct at least two stars out of five. The menu states just tamago, which most will associate as a sweet egg omelet found on sushi, but in general it just means egg. First, I will say the egg is approved. Perfectly cooked so that the whites are solid and the yolk a molten lava-like consistency. There's been so many times when I get an overcooked egg and I just want to cry. I actually always have to ask Nomiya to undercook my egg... for fear of such a thing ruining my bowl of ramen. A sliced egg would have been A+ for presentation though! Anyways, moving on from my egg problems. The broth had depth, was full of flavor, and not overly salty. Definitely felt like a homemade meal. Heat level could have been amped up a bit, but the ground pork was soaked in a spicy marinade as well.

Overall thoughts? I would return here. It's not the best ramen I've ever had (oh, far from it!), but it's as close as Edmonton can get. Both Yuzen and Nomiya have comparable ramen, none of which are made in house. Some ramen go-ers would turn up their nose to that fact alone, but I don't mind the store-bought noodles. Cooked to the right consistency and combined with a flavorful broth, it's enough for me to return. I did enjoy the fact that a bowl at Yuzen wasn't overly seasoned as with Nomiya's, but if you're going for portion size, Nomiya's is bigger for very similar pricing ($12 at both locations, after additional charge for my egg). I appreciate Yuzen's efforts in making their broths the night before and focusing on only ramen for the lunch period. If only they can make this all the time!

Fabulous salon!  The young man who owns this nail salon certainly knows what the customer wants.  His salon is clean, and well run with friendly staff.  I've only been here twice but this is the best service I've ever had.  There is a lady there with long hair (ponytail) who shaves skin off heels like nobody's business.  Just like peeling a potato lol!  Skin was flying everywhere -- and my heels were like brand new.  Also got some art painted on two toes -- not only was it gorgeous, it was so reasonably priced.  $10 for the art and $35 for the pedi.  This is my new "go to" spot for nails.  Thanks Vinh -- keep up the good work!  I'll definitely be back :)

Dear Edmonton, St. Albert and surrounding areas - MDO is worth the trip to get funky, unique, and comfortable eye wear.

The staff do an excellent job of greeting you and personally taking the time to fit YOU for YOUR glasses, making sure that you get the product best suited to your lifestyle.  They really took the time to make sure I was getting the right frame for me, which is really important considering the fact that they are on my face all day long.  I've consistently gotten compliments every time I wear one of my (two!) MDO frames, and every time I do I recommend people head to the shop!

In addition, this is a family-owned, family-run business and the quality of care is evident in the store's design and customer service approach.

Go to MDO now.  Your eyes and your wardrobe will thank you.

What an amazing find!!! The stock and style offer an absolutely stunning selection of gifts for anyone I can think and likely people I haven't thought of yet. 

When entering the store the seasonal stock makes me want to get the credit card warmed up!! Once I had a chance to wander I started considering getting a second job just so I could begin collections of not just home decor and seasonal but jewelry and clothing as well! 

Right before I forget .... they have gifts  and even complimentary wrap them !!! I might leave with a gift mixed in with everything else I buy!!!

I was a little thrown off by the fact that Yuzen stops serving sushi on Saturdays, which seems like it would be a popular time to actually get sushi! I was very disappointed initially, but after settling with the ramen that they serve on Saturdays, I was impressed with the quality of the food and the flavour. The dining area is particularly tiny and doesn't feel very cozy, but the food makes up for that.
Have been going to MDO for years and they continually go above and beyond! Great product, great staff and great service.

Very happy with the service and care Peter takes to give me exactly what I envision for my nails. If it's not perfect he'll happily redo because he cares about customer satisfaction. Looking forward to trying their pedicure service soon, I'm sure it will be great!

The name says it all, this place is awesome! The owner is by far the best person I've ever had do my nails. He is so friendly and asks multiple times if you like the length and the shape, and made them exactly how I wanted them to look. I will definitely be back!

I dropped my boots off yesterday & he offered to have them ready for pick up in half an hour, but I was leaving St A so he asked if today was good & I said yes. When i went back with my claim ticket today, he asked me "which ones are yours?" Idk about you.. But you would think the items to be picked up might be organized according to the claim ticket or by date dropped off/due for pick up... something! Anyways we found them, they look ok, I'll see how they last.
   But does anyone else remember the days when you picked your items they would be all polished looking like new?? I miss those days. Oh & I was sure my claim tag had said $11, but then he charged me $14.. So I'm not sure why the discrepancy.. But I didn't have time to ask or argue over $3. I'll see how these last before I decide if I'm going back or not.

I took boots in for new heel lifts ---was told that it would be $37.00 for replacements and was expected to pay in advance.   Did not feel comfortable with that so took my boots and will find another shoe repair.

We just came back from the Saturday ramen special. My husband just moved to Edmonton from Japan and I lived there for a number of years so we were looking for a decent ramen place. We had gone to Shikiji in Calgary, which was amazing, and had hoped to find something similar in Edmonton.

Unfortunately, despite the good reviews re. Yuzen, we were both really disappointed. I had the miso ramen, which was bland and not spicy at all and my husband had tonkotsu, which was similarly bland. According to my husband, ramen noodles are supposed to change in thickness depending on the type of soup base but they used the same ramen noodles for all the types of broth, leading to unbalanced taste. He also felt like the ramen tasted similar to packaged ramen you can buy in Japan.

It's fine if you haven't had authentic ramen (ie. in Japan) but we will definitely not be going back.  The service was good though.

Wow! This hidden gem was worth the find. Located on the way into St. Albert off St.Albert Trail made it easy and quick access even coming from downtown. Very well priced and full of flavour (highly recommend the beef tataki for an appitizer). The service was outstanding, very warm and inviting. We messed up making our order and they rectified our mistake instantly and made sure we were satisfied,  Now that's service! I can get over the flavor of our ramen bowls, the selection of extras and various choices listen in the menu made it easy to cater to our tastebuds. Living downtown we have our fair share of ramen shops but this is highly ranked even being slightly out of the way. Will definitely eat here again.
such great attention to detail, love Awesome Nails. I've never gone for a wax or tint but I have gone for both manicures & pedicures multiple times and I've never been anything short of impressed.

I went to St. Louis' recently with some friends for a night of drinks and laughs. Our experience was less than favorable. 

When we showed up, the waitress didn't take our drink order even though she came to our table to drop drinks off for our friends. We ordered a double spiced rum and coke and got 2 singles. THEN we ordered a second double spiced rum and coke and they used white rum. We had 3 waiters/waitresses switching back and forth on helping our table of 5 and sometimes no one would come help us because they all assumed the others were helping us. When we got our bill, they put it all together even though we clearly specified before we ordered anything who would be on what bill. 

Pro tip for future customers: double check the items on your bill. They added a side of gravy and other items to our bills even though we never ordered any. Definitely some growing pains in their first few months of opening.

So happy with this salon! This was my first time here. I showed the staff a picture on my phone and Vinh agreed to give it a try. My nails were thin and damaged from previous nails, but these guys were very gentle and precise. Vinh always stopped to ask if I liked the shape, color etc. The salon was very clean, all the staff were welcoming and friendly. They use liners in the pedicure tubs. Vinh is so artistic! I love the Vegas skyline he created. When I got up to pay, he picked up my coat and held it for me, while I put it on.  What a gentleman! Great service and very reasonable prices! I will definitely be back!!

Apparently they are closing soon. I hope to relocate to a bigger space, it's currently uncomfortably squishy. In the meantime, seems like no new customers are needed. Walked in, stood awkwardly at door for a bit, figured rather than staring over peoples' shoulders, went back to the waiting area. And waited. And waited. We left, never having been acknowledged.

Good luck on the new endeavour, work on your organization and customer service.

The newest place in town serving up pub food and more that's fresh and delicious. Being a brand new restaurant, everything is clean. Menu has a number of vegetarian choices for non-meat eaters.  Portions are plentiful and prices are good. They are still working out a few kinks in serving but that's a minor blip in the whole operation.  We came on a weekend fir lunch and were seated immediately. Service was quick.

Last month, I finally had the chance to check out Yuzen! I was never able to before since I always worked on Saturdays. Coincidentally, my friends had never been there either so all 6 of us were newcomers! Yuzen is a Japanese restaurant in St Albert that offers the regular food you'd find such as sushi, sashimi, bento, and tempura. They're also very well known for their ramen, which is only made on Saturdays from 11:30 am to 2 pm. My friends and I came around 12 pm and knew we'd have to wait since we needed a bigger table. Our wait was about half an hour which wasn't too bad. The restaurant itself is tiny though. You're very close to each other and although it doesn't feel intimate, there's a bit of a cozy feeling. Which is perfect for eating ramen, of course. 

All of the ramen was accompanied by the usual: cha shu, bamboo shoots, green onions,  and nori (seaweed). I was craving miso soup so I decided to go with the miso ramen, which uses a soy bean paste. The ramen sizing was decently generous, I was full after for sure! Actually, I got mad itis after. The broth was very light but it wasn't bland. The noodles were chewy in texture and fun to eat. One thing to note is that eggs are an extra addition with the ramen, so don't forget to order it. The size of the egg was surprisingly big compared to other ramen bowls I've had. 

The tonkotsu ramen had a thick and creamy broth made from pork bones. Yuzen perfected it because it wasn't too thin or thick which can be a problem! This particular ramen is more creamier so I would recommend it if you wanted a heartier meal. The shio ramen had more of a saltier base. The right touch of umami was found in this ramen, just like all the other bowls. For those with a spicier taste, tantanmen ramen will be your go-to! It uses a sesame paste which brings out the redness in the broth. The spiciness level was definitely there so this isn't for the weaklings (aka me cause I can't eat anything spicy). 

Along with their ramen menu, Yuzen also has appetizers and donburi (Japanese rice bowls) on Saturdays. It's definitely a smaller portion that the ramen so I wouldn't say it would be filling as a meal. My friend ordered the chicken teriyaki flavored which came with deep fried chicken. The teriyaki sauce was too light for me. I feel like overall the bowl lacked some flavouring and was of average. 


I wouldn't say Yuzen is the best ramen shop but it's definitely one of the better ones in and around Edmonton. Honestly, I prefer Ohana Ya in St Albert for ramen. If you ever have a chance to stop by on a Saturday, I'd recommend it. I probably won't be back till the colder season though just cause I don't really like ramen in the summer... Yeah I'm weird like that! If you decide to stop by, go before they open so there's less of a wait time. And less chance of them running out of eggs cause we got the last eggs apparently.

So here are my thoughts.... They serve Basic sushi here. It's not the worst, but not the best.  It looks like this is as good as it gets for me, as there are not too many choices in this area, without having to drive across town when I have a last minute craving .  Im beginning to realize Edmonton, and area hasn't been to other prime cities for delicious , specialized rolls, as they rate some of these sushi places 4 and 5 stars. You can call me a bit of a sushi snob. I guess I'm spoiled with good quality sushi from all my travels.

Upgrading to 5 stars because the service absolutely cannot be beat.  I've referred lots of people here over the last couple of years and they are always very happy with their experience.

The owner will greet you by name when you walk in, even if you haven't been there for a long time and he will remember the things you told him on your last visit.  The very first time I went in, I had my mom with him, and now every time I go in, he asks me how my mom is doing.

They do phenomenal work and I love showing my nails off after I get them done.

Went to this restaurant for the first time. Wont be going back. 
Our kids food came out before ours, by the time ours came, the kids were done. 
Food wasn't great but wasn't horrible. 
Service was okay. 
Nothing stood out that was horrible, the food was just mediocre. Nothing I would want to go back for.

I drove 20 minutes out of my way because it had 5 stars, took walk-ins, was open till 7:30 and was marked as $. I got there at 4 and asked for a pedicure and a gel fill. They told me they could only do a pedicure. 
Then the said it would be 5 dollars extra to basically peel the old gel from my toenails. The water was coolish and didn't reach my ankles. When she "massaged" my calf's by hitting the fronts of them she took no notice nor care of the 3x4 inch black and blue bruise that was on the front of my leg. Ouch. 
My toes were not dry when they hurried me out just after 5 so the three of them had time for supper. My one toe smudged so she reluctantly painted a couple more coats on and hurried me to the cash for $42 plus the tip I gave that I now question.
I would have been okay if the asked if I could come back after their supper or if they had even done a half decent job.
Love this place!!!! Hands down the best in stalbert. Very reasonable prices for the excellent service. Always taking the time to make my nails look perfect. Definitely coming back often!!!!!
Was lucky enough to get in right away when I called.  And I'm very happy with my nails! Had Ava and she did a great job on my acrylic fill. Will be going back!

I continue to be impressed with the customer service at this Save On location.  I especially like the produce department where the staff have offered to order me in items as well as check their stock in back for a fresher option.

The bakery always gives a cookie to my toddler with a smile.

My mom had an unfortunate experience from a young staff member at customer service and put in a comment card. Only a few days later, she received a telephone call from the store manager wanting to apologize and rectify the situation.

My toddler loves to put change into the seeing eye dog bank statue and will pet the statue and talk with him while we pay for our groceries :-)

And we continue to see Bill, the deaf gentleman stocker, who is always a pleasure to interact with. 

The lines are quick and I've never had to wait more than 5 minutes in line - 2 big thumbs way up!

MDO has been my family's optician for 20 years. I feel very fortunate to have such great family owned company here in St. Albert. They are ahead in the fashion trends, and very unique  in their approach to serving you. The staff is very pleasant, and their knowledge makes you feel comfortable from the minute you walk in.  You must go and experience this  one of a kind service!

I continue to frequent this Save On Foods on a weekly basis for Darrel's Deals and Happy Hour in the butcher department.  Tues - Fri from 3-6pm they have 50% off offerings with a Save On More Rewards account.  The blueberry maple gourmet sausages on Thursdays are hubs fave and I love the prawn skewers on Friday for $1!  Makes for a quick salad thrown over a bed of spring greens or crunchy romaine! 

In general, you've got to know your prices when shopping here because some things are 50% to even 100% higher in price than at Superstore or Costco.  

Save On has a great produce guarantee where if you don't live it or something is wrong with it, not only will they refund you but they will also send you home with a replacement. 

Another fave item here for our family are the chicken pot pies in the hot deli section - my 11 year old looooves them! 

As a mom of a young one with food allergies, I really love the free fruit option (basket in produce area) in lieu of a cookie for shopping trips. 

Also, be on the lookout for serious markdowns usually up front in a green shopping cart!

Oh and I REALLY appreciate not having to use a quarter or loonie to get a cart! 

See you soon Save On, see you soon!
Went here with the family for 1/2 price wings. Food came out quickly and was steaming hot! Good sized, meaty wings, tons of sauce and dry rub options! We were stuffed!

This is by far my favorite grocery store! Every time I walk by an employee, they graciously asks how I am doing and if I am finding everything ok! The staff is very friendly, including all the managers! The store is very clean and very well stocked! I buy all my produce only from this store! It is top quality. I love this location!

I was VERY happy with this salon.  Called in at noon and they fit my friend and I both in at the same time around 5.  They gave us both a bottle of water as we walked in and were very chatty and friendly, unlike a lot of other small salons.  The owner is such a nice man, and gave a wonderful manicure.  The salon is very clean and cozy! And the prices were amazing!! $20 for a manicure and $30 for a full spa pedicure.
Had the best burger I have had in my life. The Jalapeño burger is amazing! Great food at a reasonable price, highly recommended!

I couldn't bring myself to give this 3 stars, meaning "A-Ok" ....  because nothing was truly "Ok" about my experience.   It's a nice-looking restaurant, inherited from one we used to enjoy, but that's about it.
