There are several kind of more traditional Cajun dishes (including a red snapper and crawfish etouffee). I had the fried oyster po boy, with the bowl of chicken and sausage gumbo. The po boy was delicious, but more of a variation of a po boy. It was served on a muffaletta bun (rather than the traditional French bread) and instead of being dressed with lettuce and tomatoes it was dressed with lettuce and alfafa sprouts and was served with a dill mayo. If you're in the mood for a traditional New Orleans style po boy then this might not be the place to go it, but I thought this spin on this sandwich was really enjoyable. 

The bowl of the chicken and gumbo was delicious, and was more of a traditional gumbo (although the sausage was a mild, mundare-type rather than a spicy andouille). The gumbo has lots of flavor and a decent amount of spice. I think a bowl of soup is only $1 more than the cup, but be warned if you get a bowl of soup with your meal you'll likely not have room for any appies, or desserts. 

The food is delicious, the portions are good, some of the main dishes give the option of a petite size, which is nice), the prices are decent, and the service is friendly. Aside from the strange entrance into the building the only other issue with the restaurant is the fact the room is pretty open and sound carries quite loudly. But a little noise is worth it for some delicious food.

I love Creole and Cajun food having travelled a bunch through Louisiana for work and for pleasure.  What a delight to find that an amazing gumbo in this restaurant full of seafood, tomato-ey and thick! We also tried the shrimp bisque and it was filled with tender baby shrimp and very different (in a good way!) from the gumbo.    

For mains we tried the crab cakes (made with real crab!) with roasted potatoes and a blackened snapper dish (they didn't have catfish) with safron rice.  Both were tasty and reminded me of the deep South.  

For dessert (all made in-house), we had the pecan pie with some vanilla ice cream on the side which did not disappoint. The most amazing surprise was the phyllo wrapped cheesecake - I've never had anything like it with the freshly baked phyllo crispy and flakey and a warm smooth cheesecake inside.  

The flavours were great and the quality of the ingredients impeccable!

Definitely a must try if you like Cajun food! :)

Great for large groups. Good food. Great prices.

I've been going to cajun house for over a decade. It is my top 3 places to go to for group dining. They serve large groups the best compared to other fine dining establishments. Everyone gets their food at the same time, so it's never awkward seeing other people eat. 

My two go to dishes are the chicken jackson and the filet yaya. It's basically the only dishes I eat here bc everything else is just not that good in comparison. They are so good, my family of 14 peeps ussually only these 2 dishes! We always finish our meal with the deep fried cheesecake. It is the best dessert ever bc its loaded up with raspberry puree and white chocolate syrup. A bit of all 3 desserts mingled into 1. Cheese, chocolate, fruit... shit u cant go wrong there. I love the gumbo as well!

The food is good but its lost the spicy kick most cajun food normally has. Most likely bc it caters to canadians instead. But it's still flavourful! This is my favourite restaurant in st.albert!!! And I've worked in this town for over 15 years!

Tip: You must request the free french bread. 

It's awesome they dont require a creditcard for large group dining! And can easily split Bill's instead of 1 large bill making life easy with a large group!!!@

I've been going here since 2016 and have since been bringing my young son. The staff there are very nice and respectful. I love how they treat a 7 year old like he's a grown up. He loves the fact that he can wait his turn by playing video games or watching TV while enjoying a nice, cold glass bottle of pop from the Tommy Gunn's fridge. I love the shampoo and gentle scalp massage and the small talk conversation. They will talk to you as much or as little as you want, depending on how social you plan on being that day. It might be a little pricier compared to some of the the smaller  salons but well worth it, in my eyes. The little nuances and attention to detail is very much part of what keeps me coming back. 

Plus, I get to have a Daddy/Son outing with the boy while he beats me at Ms. Pac-Man.

If I could give this place 6 stars I would.  We were meeting good friends to celebrate her 70th birthday and she loves Cajun House.  

My mom and I got there really early. Our reservation was for 6 my mom and I finished our Christmas shopping early thought we would go sit have a drink and catch up until the guest of honour arrived.  Cajun House had no issue with our early arrival.  

Our hostess/server sat us down and explained to me where the washrooms were. I'd like to say this I have never ever had such exceptional service.  Every server we interacted with was amazingly kind and attentive.  They took our coats and hung them up.  We didn't realize until we left my mom thought she lost her glove, it must have fallen out of a pocket when our server hung it up and she placed it in a pocket with a zipper and closed the zipper.  We later realized that and were just so pleased with that attention to detail. 

Love the ambiance in this restaurant.  The menu is great.  We ordered the king brie appie to all share and it was so good. The server even offered to brings us more bread to use to dip!! What a great suggestion. 

Everyone loves their mains, mine I had the Chicken Bienville.  I found it pretty bland and shared that with our server who told me I could add whatever I want to it they would do it.  The chef said that it is the more mild main on the menu but they have no issue adding heat or flavour to it and so they did and it was fantastic.  I really appreciated that level of service.  

I will absolutely come back.
I just went here for the first time and I've already decided I'm going back tomorrow. That lemongrass  sub was just too good.

Too many gangster movies or maybe Sweeney Todd had me white knuckling the whole time! For no reason! It was a great shave, honestly closest in awhile. The whole process is fun! They pamper you with lotions and towels. I repeat it is a great shave! The haircut is also nice, they pamper you again and do a great job. It overall is just a great experience, of course you pay for it. It isn't crazy expensive but I also would do it every week. Yes I am sure I will go again. Maybe in a couple months!

Friendly crew turns out dependable--but not stunning--bahn mi and pho and other Vietnamese food favorites. Also bubble tea in a variety of flavors.

Some indoor seating, but its limited. Mostly a take-away operation.  Nice people.

The Cajun House

Mid-June 2021, this was our first attempt at a dine-in experience since the beginning of the pandemic, so we decided on trying something different than I would normally cook at home (I enjoy cooking as a retirement hobby and love to experiment, only limited by the ingredients that I have on hand).
We decided to try the Cajun House in St. Albert.

The parking lot was a bit crowded on the evening that we arrived since part of it was under re-construction, however we fortunately found an open spot.
On arrival, we were cordially greeted by a Hostess and were promptly seated in a surprisingly full dining room, though it was apparent that measures had been taken to properly space the tables according to COVID-19 protocols.
After perusing the menu, my wife and I decided on a few items that looked interesting, she choosing to start with the Chicken and Sausage Gumbo and with the Filet Mignon Ya-Ya as her main course. I chose the Bouillabaisse and the Seafood Jambalaya.

Nancy's Chicken and Sausage Gumbo was very good, thick with blended tomatoes and vegetables and bits of chicken and sausage. My Bouillabaisse was a rich and tasty broth filled with a good amount of various seafoods including mussels, chunks of what I believe were snapper, and topped with a large crab claw.

The Filet came out nicely prepared, done medium as requested with a mix of tender-crisp vegetables and roasted potatoes. My wife reported that she enjoyed her steaks, though she is not used to eating meat with a sauce quite a sweet as was the port demi-glace (she generally is not a fan of sweeter/savoury meat sauces in general) however I noticed that she finished all of the sauce on her plate.

My Jambalaya was excellent, with the right amount of spice, generous amounts of seafoods, and a good amount of savoury rice. Well done!
Needless to say, we were both quite suffonsified, and had no room for dessert.

The Cajun House provided a satisfying way to start (cautiously) eating out again.

I ordered take out from this lovely restaurant. The filet ya ya was out of this world and melted in my mouth. The second dish was the veal with the pasta and vegetables. Both dishes melted in my mouth and very generous portions. It is pretty much some of the best dishes i have ever tasted and i eat out a lot. Kudos to the chefs and my delivery came piping hot. It seem like the food just came out of the kitchen so fresh. I recommend this gem of a place to anybody that is a foodie.
Sub was so good, prepared really quick and super well priced. Definitely a hidden gem in St. Albert!

I posted a review this summer and it disappeared. Now Yelp asks me to post it again.  It is a great place for Cajun food.  I ordered the combination plate with prawns, beans and rice.  Very filling. They have a Parking lot.  There is an open atrium with nice decor and a narrow area with a view.  Nice place overall.  Kind of romantic on the narrow area. Staff were friendly.  I would try it again.

I needed to meet a friend for a coffee and chat a few days ago...decided to get to the glasshouse bistro early so I could have lunch first... SO delicious..the bacon mushroom soup was amazing! the service was friendly, the atmosphere lovely...I'd visit here more often - if I lived closer.

The Iconoclast drip coffee was delightful. Iconoclast is an Edmonton-based company that roasts their own beans and does everything by hand. The result: a gorgeous cup of Joe.

Glasshouse's Local Yogurt and House Muesli is served with house-made fruit compote. It's creamy, crunchy, and tart with every bite. For $4, you get a veritable parfait-sized portion and it's just. so. good.

The Roasted Beet Salad came with an unusual but very tasty hemp heart-crusted goat cheese topping, along with onion jam, cold-pressed hemp balsamic vinaigrette, and walnut/apricot crackers. The beets were perfectly roasted and the goat cheese added a beautiful savoury edge to the otherwise light salad.

The French Toast came loaded with smoked Polish cheese, rosemary and apple compote, and Sandyview Farms double smoked bacon. A gigantic stack of sweetness tempered with savoury elements, the Glasshouse's French Toast is the perfect way to heartily indulge yourself on a Sunday morning. You won't be eating much else for most of the day, that's for certain.

If you fancy a more traditional brunch option, try the Farmer's Scramble. Made with Sandyview Farms chorizo, local eggs, blue and russet potatoes, herbed winter vegetables, and whole grain toast, the Scramble is one perfectly-made bowl of brunchy goodness. The bistro uses good quality chorizo; you can tell the difference from pre-cooked, frozen, or cheap varieties because the chorizo at the Glasshouse doesn't taste greasy. It doesn't taste like a deep fryer. It's firm, flavourful, and clearly has a lower fat content than the cheaper versions. Chorizo 101: if you want a quality sausage, try to find an authentic Spanish chorizo with a lower fat content (less than 30%). The greasier the sausage, the cheaper the chorizo.

We feasted at the Glasshouse during this brunch session. I highly recommend it for Sunday brunch-goers; give them a call to make a reservation first, since it gets pretty busy. The restaurant also offers an everyday menu that includes Roasted Trout Nicoise Salad, Baked Brie, a Winter Jacket Burger, and Coq Au Vin. It's a diverse menu but I've no doubt of Glasshouse Bistro's ability to make it shine.
I personally love the retro look and the neon lights. the prices are more than fair and the staff is wonderful. 10/10

I love the setup of this little bistro. Located on the upper floor of The Enjoy Centre, the space is full of light and feels very open and inviting.  

I dined here for brunch and ordered the Corn Cakes, which come with a poached egg, avocado salsa and a (local) chili and fennel sausage. Delicious! Everything tasted fresh and flavourful, and the sausage was hearty and not greasy. Others at my table also enjoyed their meals. 

Prices are on the higher end, but not at all unreasonable.  I would definitely dine here again. Recommended!

My Oh my the food is SO good here..my mouth is watering as I write this review. I've had lunch here 3 times and had breakfast here yesterday and will be having dinner there tonight. I can't wait!! I've never tasted such a wonderful mixture of oils and spices. Don't get me wrong I eat out enough but there is just something amazingly delicious about how the chef puts things together. Anyone who knows me knows I'm a super taster, meaning my taste buds are literally bigger than most people's and as a result I smell and taste everything on a heightened level and this place meets my big taste bud needs!! It's a little pricey but well worth it!

I feel like the reviews for this bistro are talking about two different restaurants! People keep referring to Prairie Bistro, which makes me wonder if it had a different name and menu at one point.

I can't speak to the previous incarnation of the restaurant at the Enjoy Centre, but Glasshouse Bistro is quite nice.

Tucked away from the hustle-and-bustle of commerce that is the rest of the Enjoy Centre, Glasshouse is bright and open. The atmosphere is nice, although the service is a bit shaky. As my wife and I approached the "please wait to be seated" sign, a bartender from the cafe/take-away counter yelled at us to stop and try some wine samples. We declined (partly because we didn't appreciate being yelled at and partially because the samples weren't free) and proceeded into the restaurant.

Our waitress was generally good, but the initial experience of being yelled at from across the room put a bit of a damper on things.

The menu at Glasshouse is small, but all of the items on it look good. The drink menu is also quite good. As a fan of quality beer, I'm happy to see that they have put careful thought into their small beer selection. In addition to a variety of Canadian and international bottled craft beer, Glasshouse has locally-brewed Yellowhead on tap.

I ordered the steak sandwich. Too often, steak sandwiches are little more than a slab of meat on a toasted baguette. Glasshouse's version has sweet onions, a herb mayo, greens, and delicious fresh bread. It would have been nice if the bread was a bit thicker, because it soaked up too much of the mayo and steak juices and was quite soggy by the end of the meal, but overall this was an excellent steak sandwich.

My wife had the roasted beet salad with a side of steak. The salad was very good, although she complained that her steak wasn't very flavourful. Both of our steaks were cooked perfectly to order, though.

Most of the prices on the menu were quite reasonable. Some of the other reviews say that they were too high, but I didn't find that to be the case. I also didn't find the menu or servers to be snotty or bragging about their local ingredients (in fact, the only mention of local ingredients I noticed on the menu was that the steaks came from a particular farm). This is a major reason why I suspect that this restaurant used to have a different name and menu.

Glasshouse Bistro is a nice place for a relaxed meal after a day of perusing the Enjoy Centre. The view in the winter and early spring isn't the best, but I imagine that it would be a nice view in the summer when the greenery has returned.

I'm giving three stars instead of four or five due to some issues with the service ("Hey! Stop! Try some wine!") and the fact that my wife's steak didn't have much flavour, but I will definitely be back and expect that the experience will improve in the future.

I so love this place and the Enjoy Center! We came here on a weekend with our kids in a double chariot jogging stroller. Our kids are 3 and 1. No one batted an eye and mentioned that there were some kid's items we could order. I wanted to sit down in the restaurant so they led us to a table with plenty of space to park the stroller and brought a high chair. The servers were friendly with our kids and brought the children's meal straight away as we had requested. You gotta ask for the kid's food right away if they're hungry! The kid's pasta was a bowl of penne with tomato sauce. It was a healthy portion and could have fed me. The atmosphere, service, food and price points make us want to return for another lunch or possibly dinner in the future.

Sunday Brunch  the corn cakes wow. Mmm. The baked eggs with kale. Mmm. Everything organic and local. Make a reservation. And go prepared to Enjoy. It's the Enjoy Center. Aptly named. Service was mostly attentive. But it's not just the restaurant, it's the whole experience...shop for pumpkins after, buy some bulbs, take home some Pinocchio ice cream... stop at the wine store. Pick up some fresh bison...it's endless.

You know that feeling when Charlie goes into Willy Wonka's factory and he's a little apprehensive and excited at just how huge and magical it is? When Andrew and I stepped foot into the Enjoy Centre for the first time, that's what it felt like. 

We had no idea where the Glasshouse Bistro was. We walked in through the market and just kept walking...I kept getting distracted at the beautiful Christmas stuff on display. Finally my hunger got the better of me and I peeled my eyes away from potential gifts (for myself?) and forged onwards. Not ten steps out I spot a sign that says Glasshouse Bistro so we edge forward, looking like the rookies to this massive place that we were.

Glasshouse Bistro is gorgeous. They've got booths and tables in open space, fresh flowers at each table in cute, short glassware (I love this. Can you imagine trying to talk over a giant vase of flowers?!). There is ample space between tables so you never feel claustrophobic and can have a comfortable conversation with friends. I ordered their pumpkin seed super salad (this is not the official name) and Andrew ordered corn cakes. I almost wish I ordered the corn cakes because holy heck they were de-freaking-licious. But I'll let Andrew talk about that. My salad was no sore loser, it had pumpkin seed with chicken breast, greens, alfalfa, butternut squash, cubes of feta. It was honestly huge and packed with nutrients. The best part was it was so fresh. Andrew's corn cakes, a cup of coffee, salad, a small cup of fresh pressed orange juice, and bread pudding set us back about $65. Pretty steep for a lunch for 2, but I was happy and satisfied afterwards.

The verdict? I will definitely come back once in a while to check out their updated menus as the seasons change!

Much like a good portion of the other reviews, i was quite pleased with the design and atmosphere of the Glasshouse Bistro, but the service was sub-par at best. Our server was nice, and took generally good care of us, but also seemed to want us out just as soon as she took our plates away. I was out for a nice dinner with some girlfriends so of course we wanted to stay and visit for a bit. Our server came around to our table probably every 5-10 minutes asking if we wanted to pay our bill yet. Very annoying. 

One of my friends ordered a diet coke, and chicken club sandwich with no tomato jam or onions. I ordered the exact same and got exactly what i ordered. My friend on the other hand got a regular coke, and her sandwich had BOTH the tomato jam & onions. Mistakes happen, we get it, we're all human, but it still didn't help with our first experience there.

As this restaurant is part of a greenhouse, a little bit of "nature" is to be expected, but we had 2 good sized spiders join our table which wasn't very appetizing. On the floor right beside our table there was also a very large dead bee. The spiders are not really the restaurants fault, but again, it was part of the whole experience to which i am reviewing.

The food i thought was quite good however. As i said previously, i had the chicken club, and i was pleased with it. They have 3 sides to choose from i believe it was, i chose the potato salad. It had quite the kick to it. I had also ordered an iced tea, but they do not have regular iced tea, they have a home-brewed iced tea which is much like the only option the United States offers; regular brewed tea. It was excellent.

Overall i enjoyed the restaurant. We were seated along side the glass and had a nice view of the lake. I would go back and recommend it to others.

Weil, I must say.... I have seen many restaurants go downhill but none as badly as the Glasshouse Bistro!  They should rename it to over-priced, under staffed school cafeteria!  What an extreme disappointment our visit today was.  Piles of people were there for the art walk and some headed over to the Bistro. Well, you have to order at the snack counter then take your number, find a seat and somehow they will find you with you order.  If it is just a snack, you carry your own coffee and goodie to a table on a plastic tray.  Remind you of school?  There were dreadfully understaffed... you would think the scheduling of the art walk was a surprise to whoever runs this cafeteria... and so very overpriced.  My two comrades had muffins, one of each kind... and their comments were... not even mediocre... and so very small for the very high price. AND only 2 cookies, 2 muffins and 1 brownie type thing to choose from... they were NOT impressed.  However, the coffee is still fabulous. Yeah... some Bistro!

Amazing. Every appetizer, every dish... All to die for. Spinach and artichoke dip like no where else. A pulled pork sandwich on a brioche bun... Unbelievable. Great service and great atmosphere. Highly recommended.

This is a beautiful venue no doubt.  And it must be magical at night. But seriously overpriced -  $50 for a breakfast for two!  Without a gift card I would not have gone there and will not likely go back.

I recently had lunch at the Glasshouse Bistro at the Enjoy Centre in St Albert. 
I really enjoy coming here for brunch/lunch since they use all local and organic ingredients. 

I had the soba noodle and roasted beets salad for $14 with an Earl Grey tea. 
This was one of the best salads I've had in a restaurant in a long time! So good! Roasted walnuts, white beans were also in this salad. It was such an interesting mix! 

One thing is since this restaurant is in a greenhouse, I find the temperature can go up or down. It was quite warm the day I went with the sun beaming in. Great atmosphere though!

Wonderful ambience (bright and spacious), food (flavourful and interesting), and service (attentive to our group of seven celebrating a birthday lunch). Our food choices varied and all were very good with generous servings. Plan to spend some time after lunch to browse the shops and food stores in the Enjoy Centre. Excellent experience...we'll all be back!
Brunch was delicious and the patio is unmatched in Edmonton, a great way to spend a sunny morning! I wish they had the old cinnamon buns though... :(

This eatery at twilight is delightful.  The view overlooks Big Lake. It's a place to sit and linger...From the appetizer all the way through to the dessert. Not a place to rush, kind of pricey but enchanting

Sunday Brunch was our sole purpose for our visit and my husband and I were blown away! We were greeted by bright & friendly staff and seated quickly.

My vanilla bean latte was great, as was the carrot, apple & ginger pressed juice.

I ordered the special for the day; smoked scallop omelette with cream cheese, spinach and topped with bruschetta. Underneath was roasted yam & potato, with a few salad greens on the side. (Best omelette I've ever eaten!) My husband had steak and eggs with the same roasted veg as me and extremely enjoyed it. The prices didn't really bother us, as our only other option in St. Albert for brunch is Smittys (cheap & terrible) I don't mind paying more to support local farmers!

Coffee refills were prompt and frequent, and the overall atmosphere was casual yet a little chic.

I'm excited to go back and maybe start a tradition of going every Sunday!

Everyone needs a go-to drug store, and this one is mine. I love the location plus the store is never too busy. The best part is that the pharmacists remember who you are (I don't go regularly) and answer questions knowledgeably with helpful advice.

They have regular sales too so I like watching the flyers and then going when items I use are on sale. This location has a large selection of electronics too and the staff actually know what they are talking about so I feel comfortable asking for their advice and showing me what they mean when they respond.

I like the online photo services too. I can upload my photos online and then I am emailed when my print order is ready to pick up which is convenient.

Overall this is a great drug store, in a great location, with great staff. Plus they have great hours!

I've recently begun getting my photos printed at London Drugs at the recommendations of a few photographer friends of mine.  I had 8x10 family prints recently done at Costco for Christmas presents but was so disappointed when my red headed daughter didn't have "red" hair in the photos and her pale skin took on a bit of a greenish hue.  I spoke with a few of my photographer friends who advised that London Drugs is one of the best and most reliable place for prints in town.  Now the prices are twice that of Costco but after getting my 8x10's redone there I can see why - the paper is probably twice the thickness and the staff were exceptionally helpful and courteous in the photo department.  They also run weekly promotions in the photo department that you can find out about online by signing up for their e-mails for checking their site once a week.  The promotion is announced on fridays and run mondays through thursdays.  I'll still order things like custom calendars likely from Costco as they are done out of house but in house prints will now be from London Drugs for me!

London Drugs is the only store I know of in Alberta where you can "coupon stack" - a term known by Extreme Couponers. While I'm not into hoarding and hardly clip coupons, I do appreciate the fact that I can use more than 1 coupon for the same item at this store (as long as they have different UPC codes).  They will also ad match competitor's on top of this!  As a Mom of 2 - this is a great help for items like diapers!

The alberta beef goulash served in a potato pancake with seasonal root vegetables....mmm. Also The Winter Tart which is essentially a tartine with spinach, beet, and goat cheese, also delicious. These are selections from the winter menu. We also had an almond carrot cake dessert with icing that was lick the plate no matter how impolite good. The atmosphere of all windows, fresh flowers, starlit sky and huge space with high high ceilings is relaxing, urbane and upscale. For me, this is comfortable fine dining.  Also the service was informed and attentive without being smothering. Go on a date or go with the kids, either would be fine.

I experienced this cafe for the first time while hosting my wedding rehearsal dinner, so the "side" that I saw was really more restaurant than it was cafe. 

I called to book a reservation for 30 people, and was told I'd be called back by a manager in order to arrange this. Never hear back, so I called 2 days later and spoke with a manager - we got through some details and she advised that they typically pare down their menu to accommodate large groups (no problem, they still accommodated our allergy concerns and had a good selection for kids) and that she would email me a sample menu. 2 days go by, no email. I called again and this time I got the email.

So, taking almost a week to book a reservation is a little annoying, but I think the beautiful light-filled room that they set up with centrepeices for us made  up for that.

Food was delicious but CRAZY expensive for what they call a cafe. $22 for a chicken sandwich is pretty steep. Service was a little slow but that's to be somewhat expected when you have a group of 30. 

Overall, still nice, and I would go again, but be aware of the steep prices.

Thursday evening at the Glasshouse Bistro. Having read the various reviews we were slightly apprehensive. It is a big room with long sight lines and a great view of Big Lake. 
We were greeted by our hostess and Marie was our very personable waitress. The menu was new for the season and tonight was the first night. Marie exained that they were still experimenting with the presentation and plating. 
A small but interesting choice of craft beer and wine (samples offered) which Marie was happy to explain.
I  started with brocollini on toast and May with a beet salad. Both tasty. 
For entrees we both chose the Ling  cod. Served in a puree of green pickles with veggies and potatoes, also very  tasty. Dessert was a cream puff with raspberry dust. Small but good. Kudos to chef Shawn and our server Marie. We enjoyed a very relaxed meal, pleasant conversations with both Marie and Shawn, food and drinks were delivered in a timely manner, we did not feel rushed nor did we feel we waited too long for our food.

We had a great experience last time that we went here.  The ambience is pretty much suited for a fine class in an earthly and peaceful way type of dining. My family and my boyfriend loved the soup that we all have for appetizer, and all of us order the special that they have on that day which is "the duck" and we got no regrets for not changing our decision. The duck was perfectly cooked, the salad and oranges that comes along with it also blends along with the flavor when you put them altogether. The service was great and overall, they all enjoy it.

We had a reservation at 6pm. We were seated and we just asked for water to drink. About 15 mins later we put in our order. At 7pm we walked out. Our server never returned to tell us that the kitchen might be slower an explanation for the long wait when there were only 8 tables in the whole restaurant. 1 table of 8 had food in the whole time we were there.  45 minutes and the server never returned. We were quite disappointed as we were looking forward to trying a restaurant so close to home. Great concept, but the customer service, or lack there of, and timeliness for food delivery,  needs some work. We will not be returning.

Food is horrible. They try to be fine dining, but fall from the mark. Tart was soggy and mushy. The dijon steak was unseasoned, flavourless, wet, over baked mess. Risotto was a ball of bland under cooked glue. Sever took for ever! They were short of cutlery so we sat in front of food for 8 minutes while 3 staff ran around looking for cutlery.  This hot mess cost $55 a person and the server acknowledged a number of similar complains about the risotto, but they kept serving it anyway. No one cared that our meal was cold, or mediocre at best. No apology, no compensation, no one cares!   They just ignore you until it's time to pay. They don't forget about that.  
We had a similar experience at this restaurant about a year ago, but we heard there was a new chef, so we gave it another try. Terrible. We won't be back and it is very evident why the restaurant is struggling to stay afloat.  There is no pride in the food!  Horrible and sad.

The Glasshouse Bistro is located in The Enjoy Centre in St. Albert. It is uniquely set up as a cafe on one side, if you're just stopping by for a quick soup and sandwich; and a full service restaurant on the other. Alcohol is served on both sides.

The view is an absolute delight. Although Alberta is not quite green, just yet, the sun shining into this modern, open concept restaurant is a treat you can't find anywhere else in the city.

I ordered the stuffed chicken which was served with perfectly cooked polenta cakes and seasonal vegetables (including novelty purple cauliflower!).

Food was great. Good value for the money and a nice sized portion. The wine menu is thorough and our waitress had exceptional knowledge of her wine and food menus.

Added bonus. Most everything is local! Or as local as they can get ie. B.C. salmon. So we're supporting our local farmers and community. The herbs are grown fresh, in-house.

Overall,  a really great experience. The patio looks super cool - it's an extension of the building so I'll definitely be coming back in summer. Brunch is also served (possibly on weekends only) which would be a nice change from the same ol' same ol'.

Love having a London Drugs close by!! The new store at St. Albert Centre will be absolutely amazing to see opened and will be where my review becomes a little more detailed! 
For now though this store has everything one would need: pharmacy, post office, groceries, make up, toiletries!! I thoroughly enjoy the staff at this location and have made it a pretty regular stop on my errand routine!

Everytime I come to this cafe it takes forever to get served especially this weekend. The last time I came they opened late and there was a huge lineup. Also, they didn't have any food items out at opening time. During times of special events, they could open early to serve customers who are waiting for the special event but they do not have the foresight to try an earlier opening. This weekend I had a latte and found an eyelash in it. An eyelash. From someone's eye. I was already walking around the craft show, disgusted, so I threw it out because I didn't want glasshouse pinkeye.

I tried Glasshouse for the first time last night and I was very underwhelmed. we were one of the very few tables on a Friday night.

My friend and I wanted to try a few things so decided to order the fixed 3 course dinner and two other items. The fixed menu was good value at $35, if the food had all been good. It started with coconut mussels, which there were only four of. They were okay, but a little too "coconutty". The real disappointment was the main, sable fish served over sushi rice. The fish wasn't fully cooked. Our server kindly took it back to the kitchen. It came back, the same piece of fish (heated up) and rearranged on the plate, from the manager who made us feel that we didn't know how fish should be cooked. Thank goodness, the dessert was great. It was a banana cream tart. The pastry and cream were homemade and very fresh. 

We also ordered the beet salad, which was more of a cheese appetizer with bread, lettuce and beets on the side. The lettuce had no dressing, but the bread was fresh and the carmelized onions added some good flavour.

The last item we ordered was a cauliflower, chorizo, cheese pot which was good, but nothing too exciting.

Even though the food was underwhelming, the wine was good and our server was FANTASTIC. He was friendly and all too happy to make us happy. He took $50 off our bill which was way more than he needed to do. This is a case that proves service is just as important as the quality of food... in a great way.

I tried this place a couple days ago with a couple friends and I can honestly say it was a big disappointment for all of us. We went on a weekday so don'te be fooled by the pictures cause they offer brunch ONLY on sundays. I thought at least they would have decent food or some cake with the coffee.. NO none of that. The food was honestly okay. I have had much better. The coffee was gross. When we were ordering the lady totaled everything up before we were even done. I had told her we were still going to order coffee with our food and she rolled her eyes at us??! She was honestly so rude the whole time. She told us she would bring out our coffee and when it came she didn't even bother bringing some cream or sugar. So we had to go BACK to the front and put our cream and sugar at the table. Might as well have gone to starbucks would have had a 5/5 experience there. This place is very pretty but its such a shame that the service was so bad. i will definetly not be coming back.

We go to holes quite often, for both the gardening and groceries. So since it was a sunny afternoon we tried the bistro. First I have to say we didn't eat, only had wine but all the food they brought out looked amazing!! And smelled delish too! The wine was great and the prices were not awful... The outdoor view is very nice and the service was good to. Plus selling all local product is a nice touch. We will be back for a meal!

This place is absolutely stunning. Glass walls, tons of natural light and plant life everywhere. The food is a bit pricy to look at but after ordering SOOOOO WORTH IT!!!! Been here a couple times now and making my way through their signature menu. Never a disappointment to the tastebuds. This place has so much to offer! My only sadness in being they only offer 1 hour of free wifi/day which cuts my work sessions short as I take my laptop and like to work on my business in such a refreshing place. If they allowed more time I'd be there ordering coffee and snacks all day! Haha
I enjoyed the delicious tomato & gin soup.  A relaxing Bistro atmosphere...and warm soup tops the day on this cold day.

I was really excited to go here for brunch on Sunday. And I've been here before for lunch and dinner but I always find the service and the staff kinda meh. There was no one around when I got there for brunch and when the staff did come out they just kept setting stuff up. I ordered the eggs benny and was disappointed in it. The hollandaise sauce had almost no flavour too it and the English muffin was toasted so much I had to saw through it. The presentation of the food was good but I wish the service was a lot better. It's such a beautiful spot to eat.

I came here yesterday with friends while attending the Make It Fair in the same building. As there are limited dining options in this building, my friends and I headed to this cafe to grab a warm drink and a snack to tie us over until our late supper date. While waiting in line to order our drinks, I see an employee of the cafe come out to change the sign on the counter to indicate the cafe was now closed. No biggie, since we were the last people in line with a small handful in front of us. 

Shortly afterwards, a young gentleman comes up to us to let us know the cafe is now closed and that WE had to let anyone else know who showed up after us that it was now closed. Um... excuse me?  That was very off putting and it definitely wasn't OUR job to let customers know they were out of luck. In any case, we did as we were told and had to let some customers know we were the last to be served. 

Once we made it to the counter, I asked the young lady behind the till if the pastries could be warmed up since they were made early that morning, and it was now 7pm. She replied that no it was not possible to heat them up. Because of this, I didn't order the croissant, and instead grabbed a cookie from the front counter that was prepackaged and a whopping $3.50. I also ordered my warm drink. My next  friend after me ordered the same thing as me because of the fact that the pastries couldn't heated up. And lastly, the third friend in the group asked the same thing (unknowingly) since she wasn't close enough to hear my original question, and was told by the young man earlier, who happened to be near the till at the time, that yes it was possible. By this time I was already waiting around the corner to get my warm dirnk when I heard her response. Oh how infuriating!!!!!! How hard is it to either give someone the right answer or stop being so lazy because it's the end of the day???  My overpriced cookie was almost double the cost of the pastry and it tasted horrible of course only because I knew my friend and I had been lied to. I was so mad I asked for the manager but he wasn't on call. Instead, I was given a business card to call. 

Worse customer service ever here.

Beautiful surroundings, great ambiance and so relaxing to sit on the patio on a sunny summer Friday for dinner.

From the Yellow head craft beer and New Zealand white wine to the apple crumble, everything was amazing. Our server Jackie was so fun and had impeccable timing. The boconcini salad was a work of art and so very tasty. Our main course of turkey with bread pudding and roast veggies was superb with the perfect sage balance in the pudding. Finishing with an apple crumble was the perfect ending to a great evening.

I have been remiss in not reviewing Barkers up to now. A typical trip to Barkers for Mac (my 23 month old Standard Poodle) will begin about 7:25 in the morning with me inviting him to come to work with me. Mac knows instantly that it is a daycare day and he is out the door and waiting at the door of the truck like his life depends on it. After parking in the lot at Barkers Mac makes a mad dash for the front door knowing that a multitude of 4 legged friends await him just inside their enclosed yard. He will spend his entire day there and when I pick him up 8 hours later I have a very happy and very tired puppy.

The value of socialization with other dogs is invaluable, the staff are always more than willing to keep you at ease when you first leave your four legged friend. They slowly work them into the pack and ensure the day is the best experience for your pet.

I never hesitate to recommend Barkers services to anyone. It is a great treat for Mac and is very affordable.

I have given them five stars on this review, but in reality it should be five woofs!

Not only do they board dogs and cats, but they will also board exotics.  I took my guinea pigs to board for 5 days a few years back and was surprised to find their cages had been cleaned, even though I brought them in clean :).  I will not hesistate to board them again should I need to in the future!

Dutch stayed there for a week in January 2008. The fenced-off yard in the back seemed a little cramped for such an active breed (ie. neutered, male Vizsla), but, he came home without any behavioural or health problems. The staff was pleasant, helpful and seemed knowledgeable.

Our dog is very high energy who never gets tired at home no matter how much we play/walk her. However, when we bring her to Barkers, she always comes home tired after a long day of running around which is awesome for us! They treat all pets well and prices are great too.

Always great service have been taking our pets for years, they treat your pets like their own. Finding a place to put your pet overnight is extremely hard we went to many places but once we found barkers we never looked back! We recommend for anyone especially if you are going out of town.

Love this place!  Being in the Enjoy Centre adds a specialness that can't be matched in Edmonton!  Beautiful view overlooking the vistas of the Lois Hole Sanctuary.  The menu is a combination of eclectic and comfort.  The quality and freshness of the food is hard to beat.  Most of the vegetables are grown on site (the Holes do a great job on that).  The meats are either organic or free range and come from small local producers.  The menu changes seasonally and is always great.  My most favourite meal was a lamb burger with a beet and barley salad.  Their salads are all very original and delicious, excellent soups.  Then there's the desserts - pure decadence!   They taste even better than they look and the portions are generous.  They serve a brunch on Saturdays and Sundays - awesome with house made bacon, ham and sausage.  This is a great place!

Just the worst. I came here years ago and loved it. Great good, service and atmosphere. Came here for brunch today and had to order and pay for all food and drinks at the till, get our own cutlery and bring our own drinks to the table. They walked over the food orders. 
Had ricotta pancakes which was actually buttermilk because they ran out of ricotta. It was the same price and literally only a stack of three pancakes. No fruit no potatoes no side included. Husband got eggs Benny..again no sides just 2 eggs benedict. Our daughter got one waffle because there is no kids menu..it was extremely doughy. They also ran out of hot chocolate and chocolate milk. This is a Sunday morning...you think they would be well stocked for brunch. Those 3 dishes, 2 lattes and 1 steamer came to $50. 
One person in our party forgot to get cutlery from the cashier at the counter so asked the passing worker for cutlery and he said to go to the cashier...there was no way he was getting anything for us it seemed. He appeared to be the one waiter for the whole restaurant but for what purpose I'm not sure. This seemed to be a self serve restaurant but very expensive. Our dishes were also never cleared so we started to wonder if that was our job as well. 
Overall disappointed. The pancakes were underwhelming and the waffles doughy. The eggs benedict looked delicious but very lonely on the plate with no sides. The food is overpriced for the portions. 
This place would be perfect if possibly a private restaurant took over and could hire actual servers and run like a true restaurant. 
On the plus side, the windows and natural lighting was beautiful.

BEST PLACE TO SEND YOUR DOG/CAT that I've ever seen!
I sent my 3 very shy, timid, keep to themselves, back away Pugs here for daycare and after maybe 2 visits totally changed them. They now play with other dogs, which I never thought I'd see! They come home so happy and now when I ask them "Wanna go to daycare?!" They run for the door. The floors in the dog area are heated and they can choose when to go out or in. The staff keeps me updated on how they're doing all the time. I was in Cuba and they even emailed me a photo of them. What kennel can you think of that would do that?!?! As soon as we go into the daycare all 3 of there tails start wagging and they instantly forget about me and run to the staff!! HAHA!!! 
I can't praise this place enough. Even if you live in Edmonton and its a little out of your way it's so very worth it. Changed my pugs completely, plus it's nice after daycare having them pooped out! LOL!!!

It was very sad to get a rude, unnecessary and threatening message from the staff of glasshouse bistro because I gave them a bad review. I'll post below the message that was sent to me so you can see how they treat customers! 

I think you need to cool it on the entitlement here. Who died made you queen? They open at 10 so that's what needs to be respected by you, the customer. If you wanted an iced chai latte before 10 am you should have stopped at Starbucks. And if you not getting an Iced chai latte sent you for a loop, maybe you need to slow down on the iced chai lattes. I hope your children get treated like sub human trash y stuck up prissy pieces of garbage like you. If you don't like what's being offered, turn around and go somewhere else.

My dogs were here at the beginning of Dec and they failed to tell us BEFORE we dropped them off that they had a breakout of kennel cough and although my dogs were vaccinated 3 weeks later my 8 month old puppy became very ill with kennel cough! Should have been told BEFORE we dropped them off! So unimpressed with this understandably however I do understand that these things happen

Overpriced for what it is. My drink was super small for the $5 it cost - you'd be better off hitting up a Starbucks if you wanted a fancy drink. I ordered a panini and fries, both of which were just okay. The panini was dry, the fries soggy. Not a great combo.

The once elegant and sophisticated Glasshouse Bistro has turned into a cafeteria. There has been a marked decrease in quality since the launch of their new menu in late January. A major negative change in their "service" is that they no longer serve you. You order your food at the cafe and someone brings it to you, but you have to grab your own water, your own cutlery, and napkins. The water is served to you in plastic cups, which is both tacky and unsustainable, frankly shocking environmental practice from a greenhouse. No one comes to check on how everything is or if you need a water refill or ask if you would like something else. On the food side, the new menu is very disappointing. It's been changed completely to incorporate more of an Asian vibe, but it's executed poorly. I ordered the pasta which came in a chicken broth with mushrooms. The whole dish tasted like dirty mushrooms and there was barely any pasta. I didn't finish my meal, and noticed that the person sitting next to me didn't either. My mom ordered the eggplant sandwich, which was also terrible. The bread was hard as rock and the inside of the sandwich was mushy and flavorless. The only decent thing they had were the French fries, which tasted like any other fast food outlet, but double the price. The menu is lacking in good vegetarian options altogether. Overall we were very unsatisfied with the experience. We have been going to the restaurant in the Enjoy Centre since it opened and this is by far my worst experience and the latest in a general downward trend in both the food and the service.

The next brunch location that has been conquered by Anna. Glass House is inside the Enjoy Centre (Holes Greenhouse) which has an abundant of different sections ranging from the cafe/restaurant , a market up to hosting different gardening workshops. This building is a one stop weekend getaway, where else better to spend a Sunday? The eatery itself is located to the left of the building, having a full horizontal view of the Centennial Provincial Park, granted the building itself is pretty exquisite even without the view. The space is completely open giving an airy and fresh feel, with minimal detail needed. Quite an awe-striking atmosphere that makes you appreciate a sunny day. 
West Coast Eggs Benedict - ($18.97) - 4/5 -  Cured salmon topped with 2 poached eggs on top of a slice of sourdough bread, with the star of the show being the rich hollandaise sauce. This dish is rich and savory with the little details of capers and pickled red onions adding a new level of taste with each bite. 
Bacon Eggs Benedict - ($17.97) -  
**Both dishes came with a side of Herb roasted potatoes which was probably the most disappointing lump of potatoes ever. Came room temperature, somewhat mushy  and barely seasoned. BUT the house made ketchup was amaaaaazing. Which would have been so much better if the potatoes were just as good to match. 
Service was standard; We came a little before 12pm and there were plenty of open tables so a reservation for brunch I won't deem necessary. 
I'm pretty impressed with our brunch overall, food was pretty good which only makes me want to try the dinner and lunch menu so much more! I recommend visiting if anything just for a brunch! Guarantee it'll be an eventful sunday afternoon.

Not overly impressed. The meal was expensive for what was offered. There's a menu change coming and naturally, the item I wanted to order is no longer available. The food wasn't great, the price was high but our server was adorable and made the visit tolerable. I won't bother going back though.

After a bad experience with a kennel in Nisku, we were so relieved to find Barkers. You know from your dog if a place is good or not, and our little friend was happy and relaxed after a 2 week stay, the longest he's ever been kennelled. A somewhat anxious fellow by nature, he was absolutely mellow on pick-up, not even a whine. No nasty harsh cleaner smell, a personalized report, a friendly staff and humane environment - we highly recommend Barkers!

We enjoyed the view, but your menu selection is extremely limited.  This was my birthday celebration and I have to say I was rather disappointed.  There were only 7 other people in the entire restaurant the whole evening and that in itself is not a problem but the extremely slow service, the quality of the meals was very disappointing.  Probably won't be back

I have never posted on Yelp, but I am so blown away by the people (especially Jordan) at Barkers that I have to tell the world. I've brought my dog Max to a few different "pet hotels" around the city, and we haven't had any horrible experiences, but also nothing to write home about either. 
I took Max to Barkers for the first time a month ago, and I brought his records and shots so they'd know he was up to date. I also brought his own food and some toys so he'd be comfortable. He stayed for a weekend, and when I got him back, he was super excited to see me, but had obviously made some friends. 
When I took him for his second time last week, I had to be out of town for a full week, so was a bit worried about him. The people there assured me that he would be in good hands, and boy, were they right! I picked up Maxxer this afternoon, and they had him amazingly bathed, claws clipped, winter fur brushed out (btw, this is an extra service and SO worth it for long haired dogs) He was also SO happy!! I could tell right away that he had a great time and was treated so well. 
I had missed my flight yesterday, so I called and Jordan let me know that she would make sure that Max was all clean and ready to go for today instead of yesterday. 
My dog is my fur baby, and they took such good care of him. I'd recommend Barkers to anyone and everyone.

We visited the Glasshouse for their Friday night 3 course set menu which included a salad, pork chop main, & Torte for dessert. All three were well presented, fresh & very tasty. A return visit would certainly be considered.
When the bill was presented the 2 beer that were listed at $6:00 each showed up as being $8:00 each. When brought to the servers attention she said that she would mention it to the management & left it at that. It would be advisable for the restaurant to make sure the menu & the prices be consistent.
Otherwise a very enjoyable evening.

This restaurant should not be listed as a restaurant since they don't serve a meal or breakfast anymore. 

Also, on Sunday, June 9/19, the counter server was very rude!!  As she told us that you can only get food over the counter now, much like a fast food restaurant wouldn't you say?  She had no understanding or feeling at all!!!  And was very rude instead of nicely explaining the changes. She should not be able to keep her job. 
I will not recommend the enjoy center to anyone. There is no enjoyment there

I always stop here for a treat/lunch when I'm at Holes! They have AMAZING sandwiches and treats! My fave sandwich is the vegetarian one with olive tapenade... yum yum!

They make a mean London Fog which is what I order pretty much every time. There are two giant water coolers as well so you can have as much water as you want. 

They are also ridiculously fast here so you're never waiting too long for your order.  

I also wanted to comment on the HUGE and beautiful potted trees throughout the bistro. Absolutely stunning.

This place and experience is fantastic.  Housed in what I'm guessing is a 100,000+ eco friendly greenhouse environment called the Enjoy Center, Glasshouse Bistro provides delicious, contemporary, healthy bistro fare in a stunning open concept space within the Greenhouse.  I'm guessing 50 foot ceilings and wrap around walls of glass are the backdrop for this stylish white table cloth space.  Crossing an outdoor suspension bridge takes to a semi enclosed U-shaped dining and bar deck.

The food is healthy and tasty, Lots of dishes paired with Kale and other seasonal offerings.  The Angus burger was one of the best I've had in recent memory and the short ribs looked sensational. Generous portion sizes and charming professional servers.

Aside from being a large nursery, the center, which is open plan as well, houses a health and beauty wellness center/spa, organic and natural food store and deli offering products from small and local farms, a hip gardening supply store, swank bar area, euro style coffee bar and other cool stuff.  More stuff is in the works. 

I put a word in with the big man (owner) for an indoor waterfall, so that the soothing, theraputic sound of falling water can permeate the space so we'll see what happens.  We need one of these places in Chicago.
The steak frites was delicious. definitely recommend. service was friendly and accommodating.
We recently visited Glasshouse and had an amazing evening!  The ambience is stunning and the food & service was terrific!!!

Awesome selection of small appliances for the house and great cosmetic selection. Lots of snacks and a good size book and magazine collection. Electronics is well stocked with everything you need. Staff is very helpful with finding things. Also there is a Canada Post outlet inside. And a pharmacy.

I've eaten here twice, and both times have left me extremely underwhelmed. I do not plan to return.

I stopped into check this place out as a possible location to host a bridal shower with a gardening theme. The reviews here and elsewhere were not so great, but after popping in to check out the beautiful location and speaking with the catering manager, I decided to go ahead and book the wedding shower here.

The first time I actually ate here was after I booked the shower, when my parents (who both eat gluten free due to Celiac disease) asked where might be a nice place to have a brunch. We didn't wait long for not having a reservation, but that was the only time we didn't wait. It took three separate requests to get coffee, and then cream as we were not brought any with coffee. The view overlooking Big Lake was stunning, but the service was so bad that it soured the meal. The menu was limited due to it being Mother's Day brunch, and gluten free options were not marked on the menu and the server seemed uncertain about what was and was not safe to order. We were offered substitutions but didn't get them - for example, the first course was breads and fruit. We were told we would be brought extra fruit, but we were not. The server actually joked about being a super forgetful person, which is fine at somewhere like Denny's. At what is supposed to be a high end bistro, I expect a service would doesn't giggle when he realizes he's forgotten to bring coffee after it's been asked for twice. All in all, it was nearly $150 for three adults to have brunch.  I left underwhelmed and uncertain about the upcoming shower. I wish I had gone with my gut and canceled it, and if the invitations hadn't already gone out, I probably would have.

I finalized the menu with the catering manager for the shower, and once that was done, followed up with a few more questions regarding food allergies, to which I did not get a reply. I had specifically chosen food marked as gluten free for some of the appetizers, as well as I needed to know which of the desserts were free of nuts due to allergies. I got no reply, even when I followed up twice, and so the gluten free lady decided not to attend. Also, because I did not know which of the desserts were free of nuts, I had to abstain from enjoying any of them to avoid a possible reaction. I had ordered a platter of various items and as the hostess, then wasn't able to eat any of them. Not impressed. Why not ask my server you say? Great idea - I think we saw her twice, and otherwise food runners brought out the food and didn't know the answers to any questions.  Overall the food was mediocre, and most of the group was less than impressed. Also, when I spoke to the catering manager we had discussed moving some of the plants to section off a corner of the restaurant for our use in advance, which did not happen. Last complaint, I had asked to be able to pay the bill upfront to avoid the awkward moment of being handed the bill in front of a large party, which is exactly what happened, much to the bride's embarrassment. I was pretty disappointed with how the shower turned out vs. the idea presented by the Glasshouse when I booked. 

To end the review on a positive note - the red lentil hummus is the best hummus I've ever had and if I ever did decide to return, it would be just to eat that. The location is beautiful and well designed.

Visited on June 6, 2017. My mind was blown that this gem is in St.Albert. The menu is small but amazinngggg. It felts so peaceful there. Prices are $$$, the bacon and tomato sandwich is awesome, as well as the oyster pasta. Walking around the place after you finish is also a great experience.

Went to the Enjoy centre for a Christmas market and needed some Java for such a morning. Good location by the front doors. Absolutely stunning place to sit and have a coffee with the big open atrium and window ceiling. Lots of shrubbery for fresh air and spring-like environment on such a cold December day. Nice variety of baked goods both sweet and pastry to go with a hot coffee. My latte was piping hot. Was costly enough but once seated I could have been there for hours just enjoying the environment. Latte was nothing special but not bad either. And so much to explore at the centre should you get bored of just sitting and drinking. But more awkward to walk around and try to drink coffee with a mask. Might be a nice date spot for coffee and a walk after. Overall, awesome place with decent coffee.
The sashimi appetizer was fresh and the unagi donburi was delicious! They were nice enough to offer me a complimentary miso soup.

Ordered from this restaurant tonight for delivery, used the mobile app to place the order. I repeated the order as I have ordered from here before. When the order arrived it was incorrect. We made do and ate the order that was provided. I called the customer help line to let them know that the order was incorrect and during the conversation the lady at there call centre made me feel as if I did something wrong. I would recommend that if you order from here you talk to a rep as there app do not work. My order number was 20180303 1954026.

After my kids kept begging us to go to the Swiss Chalet, we finnally de cided to go. In a few words probably one if not the worst place i have ever been.It was packed, so you would think they had freshly baked chicken..well they served what it was at least day old chicken, it tasted awfull. I know is a place that I would never visit again. If I want rottisserie chiken the one from SUPERSTORE Is ten times better
The ONLY place I will go for Aesthetics. Kalina is amazing and does a great job. Highly recommended for manicures/Pedicures.

Went here by recommendation of my friends who said this place was good-good. Seared Salmon was alright, tasted like...seared salmon, a little crispy and fishy. Toro was better than the salmon, and I think only because it's belly fat, and fat is tasty as hell. We also had Deluxe Sashimi because we ain't no basic bitches getting regular sizes. We don't play no games. We also got a bunch of other rolls, like the Boston Roll that had Salmon Belly on top, it was ok but Joanne thought it was dope. All of the sushi was pretty good but the only reason it was ok in the end was that the sushi was long and thick (no homo). 

Place is located in St. Albert, and was decorated like a typical sushi restaurant with the wood panelling and such. Service was pretty good until the watiress stood around our table without saying anything, we assumed it meant "GTFO we closed 5 minutes ago."

Sal says: Just try it

Previously, I've only had take out from here but we decided to go into the restaurant and try it out. We were a group of 7 and were seated within 3 minutes, which is good in a big restaurant but outstanding at a 10 table, quaint wee place. 
Service was prompt and cordial. The menu is well laid out, diverse, and any questions were answered clearly and kindly. 
The food was exceptionally well prepared and fresh. It arrived as ordered and was really fast!
Excellent choices for all palates and appetite sizes. 
We left full and happy and the prices were about $20-25 per head, with a couple drinks sprinkled through the total. Very fair for the quality. 
Will definitely be back!

I was visiting St. Albert area and decided to try out this sushi place. As a Vancouverite, I was already used to high quality sushi and sashimi, and I felt that Sushi Park was actually better than most of the Vancouver sushi places. Their sushi and sashimi were fresh and flavourful. I especially enjoyed the tempuras as they had a very crispy coat and was cooked very well. 
The sashimi portions were generous and diverse. The tuna sashimi, especially, was well prepared unlike other cheap places that just cut them into pieces.
The sushi roles were creative and tasted excellent. I especially liked their house special role which had tons of flavour and texture. 
The waitresses had a great attitude and provided excellent services, and the restaurant was cozy and clean and had a nice ambiance.

I had a great eyebrow wax here yesterday.  They were able to fit me in for an appointment kinda last minute when I called and they were really friendly and accommodating. And my brows looked great when I came out.

Wow, St. Albert is starting to pile up on the Japanese restaurants. With Yuzen and Ohana-Ya nearby, Sushi Park is the newest kid to enter the playing field. The more options, the merrier!

Bbop and I decided to check them out for lunch on a Wednesday afternoon. The weather was hot so we decided to kick back and enjoy the patio outside. The inside is brand new (the washroom's still smell of fresh paint) but everything looks warm and inviting. I really liked their two-table patio - watch cars cruise on by along St. Anne's street. The servers and sushi chefs are all friendly and greet their hello's when you enter. Service is good but they had a bit of trouble with their English.

- Miso soup - complimentary bowl of miso soup. Standard but always a nice way to start your meal.
- Deluxe sashimi ($32.00) - we actually ordered the assorted sashimi ($17.00 for 10 pieces) but they mixed things up with our other order. All good, more sashimi (20 pieces) is always a good thing in my books. The sashimi (from top left clockwise) was salmon, sockeye salmon, tuna, amaebi (sweet shrimp), tai (red snapper) and tako. We were both extremely impressed by the quality of everything. The tako was the best Bbop's ever had. The amaebi had a hint of sweetness to it that was just perfect. These are waaaaaaaaaaaay better than regular ebi. I'm converted. They also had a couple of deep fried shrimp heads to eat and suck the insides of.

- Assorted sushi ($18.00) - california rolls (8 pieces) and 7 pieces of chef choice sushi. They gave us 3 extra pieces of sushi which was awesome. Apparently, they've been giving out a few freebies to people, which is a great way to get customers to come back. Heck, my one friend has been there four or five times in the past two weeks. The assortment of nigiri was awesome. Totally wasn't expecting the variety and quality to be this good. From bottom left going clockwise, they gave us two chopped scallops, hokkigai (surf clam), tako, unagi, salmon, tuna, tai, smoked salmon and ika (squid). The ika had the most interesting texture - a bit creamy but a weird yet somewhat pleasant texture to it. The chopped scallop was fantastic. Happy they gave us two of those to try!

Overall, we were both pretty impressed with what Sushi Park is bringing to the table. Pretty good sushi quality for Edmonton standards. Just wish they had a lunch menu/specials and I'd be here all the time!

I shopped around at multiple companies when I installed my A/C and ultimately ended up with Furnace Solutions because I found their customer service to be the best to deal with. The setting up of an appointment was easy and my in-home quote was comfortable. I was given a few options and did not feel pressured to go for the most expensive choice. The rep understood what my house needed and did not oversell it. 

The install was great - the team that came to the house were super pleasant, did not leave a mess and made sure I was comfortable with the unit and how it operated before they left. They actually weren't 100% happy with a slight rattling noise and said that they would come back to fix it (I didn't even notice it, to be honest). They came back, fixed it and all was well again. I got a follow up call from the sales rep a while later as well.

The follow up and the professionalism of the entire experience was great. I had booked it just as the summer was getting warm and was able to have it all completed in a very short period of time - whereas some companies were understocked and told me I had to wait nearly a month. I was very happy with the service and the product, and have recommended them to others as well.

I went for lunch with two co-workers today.  My two co-workers have been here before but we checked out the menu online first so we knew what to order once we arrived since we have a time limit for lunch.  There were only three other tables when we arrived at 12:15.  We were seated immediately and our waitress took our order.  She was very friendly and chatty.  The food was a bit slow according to my co-workers.

I had the 1/2 rack of side ribs with a baked potato, my entree came with coleslaw and a bun.  I was not asked if I wanted a white or multigrain bun although the menu shows a choice.  My baked potato looked like it was overbaked and shriveled up, maybe it was from yesterday?  One co-worker had 1/3 rack of side ribs with fries and it also came with coleslaw and a bun, she was also not asked if she wanted white or multigrain.  The other co-worker ordered the Hickory chicken flatbread which seemed okay and his only came with fries.

Overall the service was good, the food was okay but I thought the ribs were a bit pricey for the quality.  Next time I would try something different.

Yeah this place hits the right notes for Japanese.  Been here about 3 or 4 times already.  The fish is fresh but seem to run out of some of the items early but understandable considering they are new.  If this is still the case a year in, then I would have a real issue.  
Food - again excellent quality fish.  Not the best toro I've had but we will see if that improves.  Rolls are good, the hot night, spicy tuna and California have been on point.  The Hot Night can get a little sweet if you're by yourself but perfect for sharing.  Great tuna tataki.  Tempura is spot on, light and crispy, not a heavy batter like some places. Their teriyaki sauce is very good on the chicken, fish, etc..  Their salad is fresh and comes with a very good house dressing.  Miso soup, well... is miso soup.
Wine/Liquor - no liquor license yet.  Better get on that, that is a lot of revenue wasted.
Atmosphere - very friendly staff.  Very accommodating for allergies and very careful.  
I can see this place being our go to spot in St. Albert as their food is very good and fresh and prices are currently better than the other options.  The one recommendation I would have for them is to increase their selection of Hot Entrees.

Great place to get tires. They get the work done when they say that they will.  Always pay the quoted price.

Came in because I had a flat. Despite not being able to find my tire purchase in their system, they didn't charge me for the fix because of my history with the store.

Waiting area has stuff for the kids, TV, coffee, tea, and hot chocolate. 

Very friendly staff at the counter.

Awesome food! Great little place to meet for lunch. Whenever we're feeling like sushi (and/or sashimi for that matter!) and in stalbert we come to Sushi Park. Try the spicy tuna combo! Clean place and washrooms are nice. Nothing worse than going to a place where the washrooms are discusting...whats the kitchen like?

The newest local restaurant in St. Albert, Confections lives up to the hype.  It is located in downtown St. Albert, next door to Jack's Burger Shack.  It serves desserts and a variety of drinks.  There are so many awesome choices on the menu, so we chose a few and shared amongst our group.  The chocolate mousse was the highlight of the desserts we chose, although the other desserts were just as amazing.  For kids, there is a wonderful option of a simple milk and cookies.  But, the cookies are made fresh to order, so they come out piping hot!  Confections also does custom cakes.  Think Cake Boss type cakes!  We viewed their picture album of cakes and were simply wowed.  This is definitely an impressive place and worth the visit.  Prices are very reasonable for what you get.

I try to go here at least once a week because the sushi is the best I've ever had. I'm from Ontario and lived out here for a couple of years now and when I go home nothing compares to the amount and freshness of this place. Hands down thr best sashimi I have ever had. The salmon and tuna melts in your mouth. The rolls are unique and delicious. All the free food they offer to you before your main course comes out is unheard of. The only bad thing I can say about this place is I won't
 be able to have sushi park when I go back to Ontario.

Came on a Tuesday around 7pm and were the only people in the restaurant. There were a few tables when we left, but a slow night for sure.

Service was extremely slow even though it was quiet. We had to wait quite a while for our orders to be taken, a long wait for food, and after waiting a really long time for the bill, we eventually went to pay at the counter. 

We were given a portion of salmon collar as a free appetizer and it was hot and crisp fried on a bed of salad. Also ordered the spicy agedashi tofu which were small cubes of deep fried tofu in a sauce with a drizzle of hot sauce. I also had a miso soup since it was on special for $0.99 but found it very bland, though a nice way to warm up since our table was right over the a/c vent.

Sashimi was fresh as was the sushi we ordered. We also tried three rolls: B.C. which is salmon skin, Hot Night which is a dynamite topped with spicy tuna and tempura crumb, and Finger Sticks which is a deep fried roll with salmon and crabmeat. The rolls were ok, but out of all of them, we really like the Hot Night. There seemed to be a lot of rolls with cream cheese in it, which was a huge turn off for me.

Average prices, average food, slow service. I'd go if I was craving sushi and in the neighbourhood, but if I was up for a drive, there are better options.

They will rip you off!  Quoted me almost $2000 in work. When I phoned to say I would not be getting the work done there, they tried to tell me that they should not "let me car on the road!"  I went for a second opinion and ACTUALLY only needed $800 of work. Talk about a HUGE difference!!  Not cool.

So delish !! Nothing fancy on decor, but flavour, quality is all there.  Service was excellent, every dish superb!! Best sushi from Edmonton and St. Albert combined!  I can't give this place enough praise .. But selfishly I hope they don't get busy but I can't see how I can keep this place secret.
Unbelievably rude staff . And restaurant not overly clean . I'm amazed they can have any business at all while being that rude . Food was ok but chicken cold . Will not return ever .

They screwed me over. Got one new Hankook all-season tire in winter for $250. Waited sooo long for them to go get one. The next morning that wheel had jammed. The tire got dragged around making a screeching sound and smelling of burning rubber. Needed to replace the tire again, for which I was charged full price less $20 for their preferred brand, Goodyear. They probably weren't diligent in their job to ensure nothing would jam or stick especially considering it was well below -10°C. That tire has incidentally been the one with the flats, and worse, slow leaks, which they fix for free if you buy their preferred brand. So, $500 for one tire and a lot of pain.

First visit, went for lunch with the girlfriends on a Tuesday at 11:30. Seated promptly by the friendly waitress. 
   Ordered Alaska rolls, BC rolls, Hot nights rolls, kappa maki, and some others I cannot remember along with 3 waters. Everything came out very quickly. It was all delicious, and fresh! The Alaska roll is to die for! We were even sent an appetizer of fried tofu, compliments of the chef.
     It was a fabulous lunch, they made a great first impression. I would consider this the best sushi place in the Edmonton surrounding area, I recommend it to all of my friends and will return again!

My wife laughs at me, but when I am looking for comfort...here is where I go.  I love the smell and the knowledge of how it will taste before it arrives.
The lady at the front seems to think she knows my wife, so she greets us like long list friends, we are seated quickly, and the food arrives so quick it can be shocking.
The beer (love my beer!) is so cold it is a joy.
I will go back as often as my wife will let me!

One of our 2 twenty + year old house furnaces quit working when the temperatures were really cold outside and we decided to replace both with one high efficiency furnace.  Furnace Solutions was recommended by a colleague who had some work done, so I called Furnace Solutions and a few other companies in the area for a quote.  2 companies made time to come out the following day to give a quote, the others could only make time a few days later.  The sales guy that came to our house was professional, courteous, knowledgeable and didn't try to sell  us stuff  we didn't need.  Their price was the best of the 2 that day and they said, because of the cold conditions outside, they would be able to install the next day. 
The next day the install team showed up on time, worked hard turning 2 furnaces into one, and did a magnificent and clean job, doing the little things that other companies may not do.  
There was a minor issue with some silicone pulling apart, they were out the next day to fix.  I am really happy with Furnace Solutions from start to finish. 
Professional, courteous, true to their word, good pricing, with an attention to detail. Highly recommended.
This place is wonderful! they always give out complimentary rolls or salads, which taste delicious. the rolls i tried ( california and a couple others) were all tasty and rich with flavor.

Had my family out to dinner last night at Sushi Park.

1. Staff very friendly and welcoming ( I had my son 2yr) and we were seated at a great table.
2. Ordered our food quickly, they brought out Green tea and Miso soup while we waited.
3. The FOOD! As each piece came out, our mouths were watering.

Sushi Park was a fantastic place to go. Great with families and small children, the food was great and the staff was warm and welcoming.

I'll be going again.
Amazing service, and super good sushi. My wife and I judge all other sushi places against this place and Sushi Park always wins! No competition for this place!

I've been there few time with my wife and we have never been disappointed. Since we move to Edmonton 3 years ago, we've been trying to find a sushi place that meet our expectations. I can say we found it at Sushi Park. Every roll is so good and salads. Great sushi place!

I went her today and had by brows waxed and got shellac (gellish) polish on my fingers and toes. I really like the result, my eye brow's look great and so do my nails!
